The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the costs of the Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise a comprehensive gap analysis of EFL's National Control Centre (NCC) at Vuda Back Road, Nadi, and the definition of an initial design and modernisation roadmap for a future NCC capable of securely operating the Fiji grid at high levels of variable renewable energy penetration. EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, serving Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Demand on the main VLIS grid currently exceeds 213 MW and is expected to exceed 300 MW within ten years, while EFL's Renewable Energy Roadmap targets the installation of 165 MW of solar capacity and over 40 MW of battery energy storage within five years. The NCC's current infrastructure, systems and operating procedures must be assessed against this future state.

 

The Services will cover:

  • assessment of the current SCADA/EMS infrastructure, data acquisition and analytics capability, and communications infrastructure (telemetry, fibre/OPGW, microwave, backup systems), including latency, signal loss and failover readiness;
  • evaluation of operational processes and readiness, including SOPs for normal and emergency conditions, demand and generation forecasting, grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability), AVR and load frequency control performance, management of distributed energy resources and low-inertia conditions, disaster recovery and black-start coordination;
  • review of grid code and regulatory compliance against international standards and good practice, and delivery of a reviewed grid code document;
  • assessment of cybersecurity for operational technology and IT, and of physical security at the main and backup control centres, against Critical Infrastructure Protection standards;
  • assessment of staffing levels, competencies, training, control room ergonomics and human factors;
  • assessment of environmental and social aspects, including energy efficiency, waste management, sustainable procurement, disability inclusion and gender-appropriate facilities;
  • preparation of a Gap Analysis Report (inception, draft and final) mapping current versus desired "to-be" states, categorised by risk level, with a prioritised modernisation roadmap, action plan, timelines and cost estimates; and
  • support to EFL to define a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy — including packaging and contract type — and to prepare the corresponding draft bidding documents.

 

The assignment requires desktop review, stakeholder consultations, site visits and physical inspection of the control room and backup facilities, and benchmarking against international best practice (e.g. IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E).

 

Implementation period: the assignment is expected to be completed within a maximum of seven (7) months from contract signature. Expected start date: October 2026.

1. Introduction & Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau & Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

Energy Fiji Ltd (EFL) operates a National Control Centre in Vuda Back Road, Nadi  on the North-Western side of Vitilevu which is responsible for real-time monitoring and control of the national electricity grid. As demand grows, and renewable energy integration increases, the current NCC infrastructure and operational procedures require assessment to ensure efficiency, security, and reliability are not compromised and are operating well in optimum conditions.

1.1    The Renewable Energy Implementation Journey

EFL is currently embarking on a Renewable Energy Implementation Journey mainly focused on Variable Renewable Energy Sources (VRES) particularly, hydro, solar and wind which is intended over the next ten (10) years, majority of it will be solar.

  • Grid Demand Current demand for main VLIS grid currently sits at over 213MW which is expected to rise to over 300MW in the next ten years. As per the current Renewable Energy Roadmap,
  • Target Capacity: Under the current Renewable Energy Roadmap, EFL aims to install 165MW of solar capacity alongside 40MW+ of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) over the next 5 years

Modernized equipment is vital to ensure continuous forecasting, real-time grid stabilization, voltage management, and optimal battery dispatch to protect power grid inertia and prevent blackouts.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to identify technical, operational, and structural gaps between the NCC’s current capabilities and the required "future state". The future state must support a modern, secure grid running on 90% or more renewable energy as per EFL's national targets

3. Scope of Work

The selected consultant will complete the following tasks: 

  • Assessing current SCADA/EMS infrastructure.
  • Evaluating grid security and stability management practices.
  • Reviewing operational procedures, cybersecurity, and staffing availability & competence.
  • Providing a detailed roadmap to bridge identified gaps with an associated cost to carry this out – detailed list of hardware and software requirements, and required capacity for EFL (staffing and required certification)
  • Supporting EFL to define an appropriate procurement strategy and draft the procurement documents. The consultant will assess the available procurement options and recommend a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy, including packaging and contract type, based on the future-state architecture, market analysis and allocation of implementation risks. The appropriate bidding documents should then be prepared on the basis of the agreed strategy.

 

To complete above tasks, the consultant shall perform a comprehensive, multi-dimensional assessment covering the following areas:

 

3.1. Technical Infrastructure (SCADA/EMS/IT)

  • Review the age, reliability, and functional capacity of the current SCADA/Energy Management System (EMS).
  • Generator-side response performance, including whether or not it is automated.
  • Review existing data acquisition, data management, and analytics capabilities of the NCC, including the definition of future-state data and analytics requirements to support advanced EMS functions, operator situational awareness, and grid modernization.
  • Analyze communication infrastructure (telemetry, fiber optics, backup systems).
  • Assess integration capabilities for new technologies (smart grid, renewable energy management). 
  • Test for latency, signal loss, and failover readiness across fiber or microwave networks to ensure optimum communication links.

 

3.2. Operational Processes, Procedures & Readiness

  • Evaluate operating procedures (SOPs) for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Evaluate supply and demand management, including demand forecasts and generation forecasts, for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Assess grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability).
  • Analyse compliance with grid codes and regulatory frameworks not only locally but to align to international standards and best practices
  • Analyze the center's ability to manage intermittent distributed energy resources (DERs) and low-inertia systems
  • Review automatic voltage regulation (AVR) and load frequency control (LFC) performance
  • Assess existing disaster recovery and black-start coordination procedures.
  • Identify state of the art weather forecasting tools to optimise generation mix in favour of our hydros and solar PVs

 

3.3. Cybersecurity & Physical Security

  • Review cybersecurity protocols for Operational Technology (OT) and IT infrastructure.
  • Assess physical security of the main NCC and disaster recovery/backup control center. 

Audit compliance with Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards, including electronic security perimeters and access controls

 

3.4. Human Resources & Competence

  • Assess staffing levels, skill sets, and training programs for operators and engineers.
  • Evaluate human factors, control room ergonomics, and mental workload. 
  •  Identify gaps in national energy policies or grid codes that hinder modern operations.
  • Evaluate the technical competency of operators in handling advanced grid planning and simulation tools.

 

3.5. Environmental & Social Safeguards

  • Assess current energy use, and waste management practices at NCC and
  • Evaluate energy-efficient technologies, waste reduction strategies and sustainable procurement practices aligned with Fiji’s National laws and Good International Industry Practice.
  • Assess infrastructure capacity for adequate disability inclusion and gender-based rest rooms/ablution facility.

4. Methodology

The consultant is expected to carry out the following as part of the Gap Analysis:

  1. Conduct Desktop Review: Review existing documentation (grid codes, annual reports, previous audits, processes & procedures).
  2. Stakeholder Consultations: Conduct interviews with NCC operators, management, IT, Telecom/SCADA staff.
  3. Site Visits: Perform physical inspection of the control room, hardware, and backup facilities.
  4. Review of current Grid Code
  5. Benchmarking: Compare findings against international best practices (e.g., IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E). 
  1. Key Deliverables

The outputs expected during and at the end of this consultancy are specified below

  • Gap Analysis Report (Inception report, Draft, and Final) will be prepared to cover the following:
    • Current State Description and functionality
    • Desired Future State Definition and functionality
    • Gap Identification (Technical, Procedural, Human).
    • Explicit mapping of current vs. desired "To-Be" states, categorized by risk level.
    • Modernized Roadmap, Action Plan and Budget: Prioritized recommendations with estimated timelines and cost implications. 
    • Determine if the existing building will be able to cater for the proposed upgrades
  • Reviewed Grid Code Document
  • Procurement Strategy and Draft Bidding Documents will be prepared to cover the following:
    • Assessment report to recommend the appropriate procurement strategy; and
    • Draft bidding documents following above procurement strategy, in consultation with EFL.

7. Required Expertise

The consultancy firm should be shown to have expertise in the following areas:

 

7.1. Power Systems Automation & SCADA/EMS Specialist

This core expert evaluates the existing NCC and defines the future-state operational technology.

  • SCADA/EMS/DMS Expertise: Deep knowledge of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, Energy Management Systems, and Distribution Management Systems.
  • Interoperability & Protocols: Mastery of legacy and modern utility communication protocols (IEC 60870-5-101/104, DNP3, and IEC 61850 for substation automation).
  • Grid Hierarchy: Experience managing control boundaries down to the 11kV feeder breaker level to ensure distribution grid visibility.

 

7.2. Power Systems Protection & Telecommunications Engineer

This domain ensures that control signals travel safely, reliably, and instantaneously across Fiji's geographical terrain.

  • Substation Integration: Expertise in integrating diverse thermal and hydro power stations with central SCADA.
  • Utility Telecommunications: Experience with power line carrier (PLC), fiber optic networks (OPGW), microwave links, and cellular fallback systems.
  • Protection Coordination: Understanding how modern EMS upgrades interact with existing line and transformer protection schemes.

 

7.3. Grid Code & Regulatory Specialist

This expert translates the technical capabilities of the new NCC into legal and operational compliance frameworks.

  • Grid Code Compliance: Experience drafting or reviewing national Grid Codes, specifically for small, isolated island grids with high hydro penetration.
  • Ancillary Services: Defining rules for frequency control, voltage regulation, and spinning reserves relevant to Fiji's power mix.
  • Renewable Integration: Knowledge of technical requirements for grid-connected solar, wind, or battery storage (BESS) into an existing grid code.

 

7.4. Cyber Security (OT/Critical Infrastructure) Specialist

Modernizing an NCC introduces digital vulnerabilities that must be mitigated from day one.

  • Operational Technology (OT) Security: Specific expertise in securing industrial control systems, distinct from standard corporate IT.
  • International Standards: Alignment of procurement requirements with global benchmarks like NERC CIP, ISO 27001, or IEC 62443.

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received World Bank financing for the Access to Distributed Electricity and Lighting in Ethiopia (ADELE) Project. It intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services.

The Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is one of the state-owned financial institutions providing project finance and lease financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to support the country's overall economic development. In addition to financing projects, the bank serves as a financial intermediary that administers funds and appraises and monitors participating financial institutions through its wholesale financing program, ensuring successful project implementation.

2. DBE invites expressions of interest (EOIs) from legally formed consulting firms to provide consultancy services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework.

3. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise technical assistance to the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) to design, document, and prepare for implementation a wholesale (apex) development finance capability as an institutional pillar of the Bank. The services include the design of a wholesale banking framework covering the lending model and the intermediary engagement model; an assessment of the institutional, legal, and delivery structure options for housing the wholesale function; the development of a Wholesale Lending Policy and Operational Manual and of a credit guarantee and de-risking framework grounded in an explicit additionality framework; the design of a technical advisory and capacity-building program for participating financial institutions, including a dedicated module on expanding outreach to women entrepreneurs and women consumers; the integration of environmental and social risk management into intermediary accreditation and supervision; and support to DBE in preparing pilot wholesale arrangements and the associated portfolio segregation and ring-fencing arrangements. The assignment is financed under Sub-component 5.3 of the project. The implementation period is approximately twenty (20) weeks from contract signature, with the consultant based primarily in Addis Ababa for the core design and approval phases.

4. The Development Bank of Ethiopia now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

       4.1. Relevant experience of the firm

Assignments count only if completed within the last ten (10) years and only where the consultant acted as lead firm or joint venture member – sub-consultancy roles do not count. A single assignment may satisfy more than one of the requirements listed below.

  • At least one (1) assignment on a World Bank or other multilateral-financed line of credit, apex facility or financial intermediary lending operation.
  • At least two (2) assignments delivered in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable frontier and emerging markets. For this purpose, a country is a comparable frontier or emerging market if, as at the date of the EOI submission deadline, it is (a) eligible for IDA financing (including blend countries), (b) classified by the World Bank as a low-income or lower-middle-income economy, or (c) a constituent of the MSCI Frontier Markets Index. Consultants must state, for each assignment relied upon, the country and the limb (a), (b) or (c) relied upon.

 

Assignments consisting solely of the following do not count under this sub-section 4.1: general management or organizational consulting; audit, tax or accounting services; IT or core-banking system implementation; training delivery without design content; market or feasibility studies without design of a lending framework or instrument; retail or corporate lending work with no financial-intermediary component.

An organogram and headcount by discipline are required. Evidence: client name and contact, assignment dates, team size and composition, and country of deployment.

  • The Consultant is a legally registered firm and has at least ten (10) years of organizational experience in development finance, financial sector development or financial institution advisory. Evidence: certificate of incorporation or registration, together with the experience record submitted under the following bullet.
  • Development finance, financial sector development, or financial institution advisory is a core business line of the Consultant, evidenced by at least five (5) completed consulting assignments in this field in the last ten (10) years.

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Empowered Green Pest Control Technology for Cowpea (Contract No.: GDCS-019) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on AI-empowered green pest control technology for cowpea.

I.Background

Cowpea is a major vegetable crop; however, pests such as thrips are particularly difficult to control during its cultivation. These pests can cause severe damage, including blackened heads and tails, insect holes, pod wrapping, and pod rot. Unscientific and non-standard pest control measures can easily lead to safety hazards, making cowpea pesticide residue a key focus of monitoring.

Traditional control methods for thrips heavily rely on pesticide spraying. However, the outer layer of cowpea flowers is tightly closed, while the inner layer is pouch-like, providing a natural "shelter" for thrips. No matter how the pesticides are sprayed, it is difficult to completely eliminate the pests hidden inside the flowers, failing to achieve ideal control results. Furthermore, irregular use of pesticides increases the risk of residue. Thrips are most active at temperatures of around 25°C, with peak activity typically occurring between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM. Their population dynamics and occurrence across different cowpea growth stages are closely related to climatic conditions.

Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—such as AI, drones, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to monitor the cowpea cultivation process and enable quality traceability, thereby achieving full-chain safety management from production to distribution.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

1.Guided by the goal of enhancing food safety, accurately predict key meteorological factors and other variables during the cowpea cultivation process to provide data support for large-scale cowpea planting management, thereby effectively boosting the efficiency of high-quality agricultural development.

2.Research and develop an integrated agricultural cultivation and management service model for cowpea production that covers pre-risk early warning, in-process risk control, and post-risk resolution, standardizing the full-chain safe production management process "from farm to table." Based on the actual requirements for the sustainable development of cowpea production, cultivation management processes, and product standards, establish a green pest control technology model that is adaptable to practical production and suitable for widespread promotion.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies in cowpea production, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI. Taking into account the actual conditions of domestic cowpea-producing regions, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of a "Low-Altitude + Meteorological + Sensor" Early Warning Model for Cowpea Growth and Pest/Disease Risks

Develop an information model for cowpea growth anomalies by modeling the nonlinear relationships between various meteorological factors and crop growth status across different growth stages. Based on high-resolution agricultural meteorological data from satellite remote sensing, and combined with ground sensor data monitoring temperature, humidity, light, rainfall, and soil moisture, quantitatively analyze and predict the risks to cowpea growth caused by abnormal climatic conditions—such as drought, low temperatures, and high temperatures—over large-scale planting areas for the next 7 to 15 days.

Furthermore, as thrips are currently the primary pest threatening cowpeas, with an optimal activity temperature of approximately 25°C and specific occurrence patterns across different growth stages, a quantitative database for crop pest and disease risks will be established. This involves modeling the risk probability of pest and disease proliferation based on different cowpea phenotypes under varying meteorological conditions. Integrated with large-scale crop growth stage estimation technology, this system will analyze the occurrence probability of major pests and diseases, such as thrips, thereby enabling proactive prevention.

3. Research and Application of Intelligent Crop Monitoring and Precision Fertilizer & Pesticide Management Technologies for Cowpea Cultivation

Based on the application research of systems including precision agricultural meteorological forecasts, crop growth estimation models, and risk early-warning models, this task aims to develop and demonstrate a precision pesticide application technology system integrating pest monitoring with fertigation (water and fertilizer integration). The study will apply efficient UAV-based pest monitoring technology to achieve early detection of pests and diseases, and conduct research on adjusting water and fertilizer agronomic practices and pesticide management based on the risk early-warning models. Demonstration bases will be established to continuously track and monitor the effectiveness of pest control and eradication through technology integration. The study will evaluate the pesticide reduction effects and cowpea compliance rates, and formulate standard operating procedures (SOPs) for precision management in cowpea production.

4.Exploring Adaptable Technologies and Establishing Screening Mechanisms Centered on Core Green Pest Control Issues for Cowpea

Intelligent Pest Monitoring Technology: Develop an intelligent pest monitoring system combining trapping with AI image recognition. This system is based on a deep vision pest identification system and integrates trapping data from yellow and blue sticky boards and sex pheromone lures with meteorological models. It will dynamically predict pest population density and optimize pesticide application windows.

Multi-source Integrated Pest Management (IPM): Screen for highly efficient natural enemy resources and establish a synergistic pest control model integrating "physical + chemical + biological" methods. Dynamically trigger differentiated, balanced pest control prescriptions to build an optimal closed-loop control model for pest and disease monitoring.

Screening of Precision Fertilizer and Pesticide Control Technologies: Establish a screening mechanism based on the criteria of environmental friendliness, economic feasibility, and operational convenience. Combined with the adjustment of water and fertilizer agronomic practices and pesticide management based on risk early-warning models, this will quantitatively evaluate the pesticide reduction effects and cowpea compliance rates.

5.Development of an Integrated Technical Scheme for "Monitoring - Early Warning - Control - Feedback"

Perception Layer: Utilizing a three-dimensional monitoring network composed of satellite remote sensing data analysis, UAV inspection data collection, and IoT sensors, the system will push real-time pest control recommendations via mobile apps or mini-programs.

Decision-Making Layer: Output dynamic pest control thresholds through a multi-factor coupled early-warning model integrating "cowpea growth stages, meteorology, and pests/diseases." Build an agronomic decision-making engine driven by an expert knowledge base to automatically generate parameterized solutions, such as pesticide mixing concentrations and UAV flight altitudes.

Interactive Feedback Layer: Through a mobile mini-program, provide three core functions: risk early-warning push notifications, an AI diagnostic assistant, and blockchain-based authentication for agricultural operation records.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Economic Cost Analysis

(1) Multi-dimensional Effectiveness Evaluation

Ecological Benefits: Monitor the reduction rate of chemical pesticides, the survival rate of natural enemy insects, and changes in soil organic matter content.

Quality and Safety: Compare the pesticide residue compliance rate, commercial fruit rate, and traceability information completeness between demonstration fields and conventional planting areas.

Economic Benefits: Calculate the per-mu income increase (premium for high-quality fruits + savings on agricultural inputs) and the reduction in labor costs.

Technical Adaptability: Conduct regional verification in major producing areas to analyze the technological adaptability across different climatic zones.

(2) Economic Cost Analysis of New Technologies in Cowpea Production and Quality Safety. Conduct a comparative analysis between cowpea planting plots within or near the demonstration bases that utilize the new technology and conventional plots that do not.

7. Promotion and Application

Technology Validation Phase: Establish two core demonstration bases in the main cowpea-producing areas of the project pilot city. These bases will be equipped with UAVs, IoT sensors, and intelligent pest monitoring and forecasting equipment. Comparative trials of "AI-based Pest Control vs. Traditional Pest Control" will be conducted. Additionally, an AI Technology Operation Manual for Green Pest Control in Cowpea will be compiled, and training courses covering scenarios such as pest identification and equipment operation will be developed.

Basic Requirements for Cowpea Planting Demonstration Bases: The open-field planting area must be no less than 10 mu. ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO DEVELOP THE NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR DEVELOPMENT OF STATISTICS (NSDS) OF SOUTH AFRICA- BW-SADC-563161-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/460

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 9 September 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model (Contract No.: GDCS-020) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on the AI-based digital standardized aquaculture technology model.

I.Background

As a vital component of China's agricultural economy, the aquaculture industry is a key sector for ensuring food security and optimizing dietary structures. With the continuous upgrading of consumer demands for aquatic product quality and increasingly stringent ecological and environmental protection policies, the traditional extensive aquaculture model can no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development. Particularly in terms of quality and safety supervision, aquaculture still faces prominent challenges, such as opaque production processes, delayed risk early warnings, and difficulties in tracing key indicators.

Due to its unique industrial characteristics, aquaculture still exhibits significant shortcomings in digital supervision practices. On the one hand, the dynamic and ever-changing aquatic environment involves multi-dimensional spatial interactions across the upper atmosphere, surface water bodies, and underwater ecosystems, making it difficult for traditional single monitoring methods to achieve full-scenario coverage. On the other hand, aquatic activities are characterized by concealment and suddenness. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from limited scope, untimely information acquisition, difficulty in identifying hidden behaviors, insufficient data accuracy, and high labor costs. These issues make the establishment of a standardized aquaculture system an urgent priority.

The core of this research lies in utilizing modern information technologies to achieve intelligent management of agricultural product quality and safety. Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—including AI, big data, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to continuously improve the regulatory system. This is particularly crucial for process supervision and quality traceability in aquaculture, aiming to achieve full-chain safety management from production to distribution. This will not only help enhance the market competitiveness of agricultural products but also lay a solid foundation for the sustainable development of agricultural product quality and safety.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

To address the current issues in aquaculture, including restricted information collection, delayed acquisition of key indicators, and the difficulty of tracing growth processes that lead to insufficient quality and safety, this project proposes to carry out the Development of an AI-Based Standardized Aquaculture System. Building upon existing development advantages and targeting the modernization of aquaculture, the project will dynamically monitor the growth status of aquatic products and implement timely interventions. This will continuously enhance product quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI, in aquaculture production. Taking into account the actual conditions of the aquaculture production areas in the project pilot city, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of Intelligent Recognition Algorithms for Aquaculture Status Based on Low-Altitude Sensing Technology

Utilize drones to capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with deep learning technology, accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics. The study will precisely extract the intrinsic correlations between image features and aquaculture status, effectively addressing the issues of untimely and imprecise perception in traditional monitoring methods. This will significantly enhance the timeliness and accuracy of aquaculture status monitoring, providing robust algorithmic support for the intelligent management of aquaculture.

3. Development of a Big Data-Driven Standardized Digital Aquaculture Management System

Integrate multi-source data to comprehensively analyze aquaculture growth processes, feeding records, and growth status early warnings, thereby achieving the digitalization of the aquaculture process. Meanwhile, based on time-series analysis and observation, monitor aquatic product quality in real-time and implement timely interventions to continuously provide quality and safety recommendations throughout the production process. Comprehensively map the complex relationships among the water environment, meteorological conditions, biological status, and aquaculture farming operations to establish a standardized digital aquaculture system. This will realize full-process digital and information-based management of aquaculture, thoroughly resolving industry pain points such as unsmooth information flow and untimely farming operations. Ultimately, it will ensure the quality and safety of aquatic products across the entire chain from source to terminal, driving the high-quality development of the aquaculture industry.

4.Exploration and Screening of New Technologies

Develop aquaculture status recognition algorithms that integrate remote sensing with low-altitude sensing. The remote sensing analysis will utilize drones to dynamically and automatically capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with remote sensing technologies for aquaculture environment analysis, the system will accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics, thereby achieving refined aquaculture status recognition.

Screening Criteria: Focusing on core indicators such as technological maturity, cost-effectiveness, and environmental adaptability, the optimal technology portfolio will be determined through laboratory simulations and pilot validations.

5.Development of an Integrated "Space-Air-Ground-Water" Technical System

Hardware Layer: Deploy a satellite remote sensing monitoring network, UAV inspection systems, and IoT water quality sensors to achieve full-dimensional dynamic tracking and identification of aquatic product status and the environment in the production areas.

Platform Layer: Utilize an aquaculture big data cloud platform to integrate a multi-source data fusion engine, AI analysis modules (such as density recognition and disease prediction), and a visual decision-making dashboard, supporting synchronized access via both PC and mobile clients.

Application Layer: Implement an intelligent decision-making system. Based on inversion models and growth prediction algorithms, it will automatically generate agronomic recommendations such as feeding amounts and water replacement cycles, and push them to farmers via mobile apps or mini-programs.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Promotion & Application

Multi-dimensional Evaluation: Quantify evaluation indicators such as the water quality compliance rate and disease incidence rate. Select two typical aquaculture demonstration sites in the Pearl River Delta to conduct application demonstrations. Verify the technological effectiveness through comparative trials, thereby providing a complete technical solution for the Guangdong Aquatic Product Quality and Safety Enhancement initiative. This will strongly drive the digital transformation and high-quality development of the aquaculture industry, demonstrating robust competitiveness and development potential in the era of the digital economy.

Basic Requirements for Aquaculture Demonstration Bases: The pond aquaculture area must be no less than 200 mu. Bases must establish an agricultural product quality and safety management system in accordance with the law, produce in compliance with relevant agricultural product quality and safety standards, and maintain digitalized production records for agricultural products.

MINISTERE DE L’EAU,

Nom du Projet : Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable.

Crédit IDA n° 71210

Reference STEP: MG-MEAH-571200-CS-INDV

Intitulé : Recrutement d'un Consultant Individuel en appui au MEAH pour l'Élaboration du WASH Compact National de Madagascar.

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar, par le biais du Ministère de l’Eau, de l’Assainissement et l’Hygiène a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), dans le cadre de mise en œuvre du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable (PAAEP Madagascar), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Consultant Individuel en appui au MEAH pour l'Élaboration du WASH Compact National de Madagascar».
  2. L'objectif principal de la mission du Consultant Individuel est d'accompagner le MEAH dans la finalisation d'un Compact National WASH de Madagascar, document politique de haut niveau qui formalisera les engagements du gouvernement et de ses partenaires en matière d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène à l'horizon 2030.

Conformément aux exigences minimales d'un WASH Compact dans le cadre de Water Forward, le document devra couvrir au minimum les trois dimensions suivantes :

  • Cibles d'accès réalistes : objectifs quantitatifs et géographiques d'accès à l'eau potable, à l'assainissement de base et à l'hygiène, à l'horizon 2030, déclinés par milieu (urbain/rural) et par groupes de population vulnérables.
  • Réformes de gouvernance et d’amélioration du secteur : actions, réformes, politiques, programmes ou textes législatifs à engager ou à finaliser d'ici 2030, en s'appuyant sur les acquis récents (PNEAH, OREA, Code de l'eau).
  • Engagements financiers : engagements budgétaires du gouvernement et plan de mobilisation des financements internes et externes, chiffrés par sous-secteur (eau, assainissement, urbain, rural, …) nécessaires pour atteindre les cibles.
  1. L’UGP MEAH du projet PAAEP invite les candidats admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir leurs prestations pour la mission décrite ci-dessus. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’elles possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services, A cet effet, le dossier de candidature devra comprendre : un CV détaillé avec les expériences et les références pour des missions similaires, une lettre de motivation avec propositions financières, personnes références avec contacts, les photocopies des certificats de travail, attestations d’emploi, certificats ou attestation de formations et les photocopies des diplômes les plus élevés.

 

Profil du consultant :

  • Diplôme universitaire avancé (Master ou Doctorat) en politique publique, économie du développement, ingénierie de l'eau, gestion de l'environnement ou domaine connexe.
  • Minimum 10 ans d'expérience dans le domaine de l'eau, de l'assainissement et de l'hygiène, incluant des missions dans des pays en développement, de préférence en Afrique subsaharienne.

 Expériences et compétences souhaitées

  • Expérience avérée dans l'élaboration de documents de politique ou de stratégie sectorielle WASH (politique nationale, plan sectoriel, compact, plan d'investissement, etc.) ;
  • Bonne connaissance des mécanismes de gouvernance du secteur WASH et des enjeux de régulation des services d'eau et d'assainissement ;
  • Connaissance des cadres de financement du secteur WASH (budget public, financements multilatéraux, financement climatique, PPP) ;
  • Expérience en facilitation de processus multi-acteurs et d'ateliers de concertation ;
  • Connaissance de l'initiative Water Forward de la Banque mondiale et/ou d'autres initiatives similaires (SWA, Mission 300, etc.) est un atout ;
  • Connaissance du contexte WASH à Madagascar et dans la région Afrique de l'Est et australe est un atout.

Langues

  • Français : maîtrise parfaite à l'écrit et à l'oral (obligatoire).
  • Anglais : bonne maîtrise souhaitée.
  1. Le Consultant Individuel sera sélectionné suivant la méthode de sélection d’un consultant individuel (CI) en accord avec les procédures de la Banque Mondiale définies dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés par les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI), de la Banque mondiale en date du juillet 2016, mise à jour en septembre 2023 (5ème édition) ;
  2. Les Termes de Références (TDRs) pour la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet du projet mentionnés ci-dessous : www.paaep.mg   
  3. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française, doivent être envoyées par voie électronique à l’adresse électronique suivante : procurement.meah@paaep.mg au plus tard le 23 SEPTEMBRE 2026 à 16 heure (heure locale), ou d’un dépôt en version électronique à l’adresse ci-dessous et portant la mention obligatoire : « Recrutement d'un Consultant Individuel en appui au MEAH pour l'Élaboration du WASH Compact National de Madagascar ».
  4. L’adresse à laquelle il fait référence est :

Bureau du projet PAAEP - Bâtiment A1, Rez-de-Chaussée, Explorer Business Park (ex-village des Jeux) Ankorondrano 101 Antananarivo - Madagascar.

Adresse courriel : procurement.meah@paaep.mg

Site web : www.paaep.mg

TERMS OF REFERENCE

To ensure the smooth implementation of consulting services for the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project , and to guarantee the achievement of the project's informatization goals, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to engage a third-party service provider to carry out the project implementation.

I. Project Background and Description

The World Bank-funded China Food Safety Improvement Project aims to enhance national and local food safety management and reduce food safety risks along selected value chains. At the national level, the project will be jointly implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (MARA). At the local level, it will be carried out by the Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation, and the Bureau of Ocean Development and Fisheries of Yantai City, Shandong Province. The loan agreement for the project entered into force on March 21, 2024. The project has an implementation period of five years, with a closing date of March 31, 2029.

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation takes the comprehensive enhancement of modern food safety governance capacity as its core objective in this project. By systematically constructing and collaboratively advancing six sub-projects, it precisely supports and effectively drives the achievement of the project goals. The Guangdong Provincial Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of USD 10 million for this project. The main construction contents of the project include:

1. Building a full-chain traceability platform ("Scan-to-Trace") for key food categories, achieving full-chain traceability and risk early warning through 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

2. Building the "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" system, providing intelligent video supervision for scenarios such as elderly care canteens and school cafeterias;

3. Upgrading the emergency real-time dispatch and command system to improve the emergency response mechanisms for food safety incidents;

4. Implementing a capacity building program for food-related personnel in the field of market regulation, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of video content for 75 courses, and skills competitions;

5. Establishing a high-quality food standards system and promotional campaigns, developing no fewer than 30 standards within two years and conducting quality monitoring;

6. Providing professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

II. Project Objectives

To meet the demand for professional consulting services throughout the entire implementation process of the World Bank-funded Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, strengthen project process management, facilitate the smooth progress of various tasks, and promote the efficient implementation of the World Bank project, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to engage a professional project management consulting agency. The agency will provide consulting services in project management, procurement management, contract management, monitoring and evaluation, and informatization management, as well as daily English translation services and the issuance of corresponding outcome reports.

This project takes the comprehensive enhancement of modern food safety governance capacity as its core objective. By systematically constructing and collaboratively advancing six sub-projects, it precisely supports and effectively drives the achievement of various core performance indicators:

At the outcome indicator level, relying on the deep integration and linkage of the "Scan-to-Trace" full-chain traceability platform, the "Internet Plus Open Kitchens" intelligent supervision system, and the emergency real-time dispatch and command system, a full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early warning response, and disposal closure will be established. This will provide a solid data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating the "proportion of warnings with mitigation measures initiated."

At the output indicator level, through the capacity building program for food-related personnel, systematic training will be provided to food safety inspectors and regulatory personnel, and the proportion of female regulatory personnel participating will be quantified. Through the high-quality food standards system construction project, no fewer than 30 standards will be developed, 6 demonstration model enterprises will be built, and 700 batches of quality monitoring will be completed. These will directly support the realization of key output indicators such as the "number of enterprises receiving project support to improve food safety management."

Through the project consulting services, the technical feasibility, economic rationality, and environmental and social sustainability of the project will be ensured, and the project design and implementation capabilities will be enhanced. Meanwhile, the consultants will assist in identifying potential risk factors of the project, propose corresponding mitigation measures, and strengthen project risk management capabilities. Furthermore, it will ensure that the collection, accounting, and reporting of all indicator data comply with World Bank specifications, thereby enhancing the international compliance and transparency of the project, facilitating the smooth progress of various tasks, and promoting the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

III. Service Overview

The total investment amount for this project is RMB 1.4147 million.

(I) Scope of Services

During the implementation period of this project, the service provider shall provide comprehensive professional consulting services to the project implementation unit and assist in the smooth progress of various construction projects.

(II) Service Content

1. Project Management Consulting

Assist the Project Management Office (PMO) in collecting and organizing World Bank-related policies and materials: Collect and organize World Bank policy documents related to project management, provide policy interpretations, and ensure that the project implementation team has a clear understanding of the policies to offer policy consulting for project execution. Assist the PMO in establishing operational procedures and detailed management system rules for this project, ensuring compliance with World Bank and national requirements, and determining management workflows. Assist the PMO in organizing preliminary historical data related to this project to provide necessary references for subsequent implementation. Be responsible for daily liaison work, including communication with the World Bank team, the Provincial Development and Reform Commission, the Provincial Department of Finance, and other relevant departments, as well as various project construction service agencies.

Meanwhile, based on project management needs, be responsible for drafting annual work plans, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project progress reports, annual comprehensive evaluation reports, daily liaison work, mid-term evaluation and adjustment reports, and training work plans.

2. Procurement Management Consulting

Assist the Project Management Office (PMO) in preparing procurement plans, drafting Terms of Reference (TOR), reviewing bidding documents, supervising bid evaluations, and managing contract negotiations and performance. This is to ensure that procurement activities adhere to the principles of economy, efficiency, transparency, and fair competition, thereby reducing compliance risks and guaranteeing the compliant use of project funds and smooth project implementation.

3. Contract Management Consulting

Assist the PMO in formulating an overall procurement plan aligned with the project construction content based on project activities, and make timely adjustments according to project progress and requirements from all parties. As requested by the PMO, assist in drafting the TOR for consulting service activities required for this project, revise and improve them according to the World Bank's feedback, and obtain the Bank's "no objection." Assist the procurement agency in handling various matters during the bidding process and reviewing project procurement bidding documents, and assist the PMO in responding to and implementing the World Bank's feedback on the review of bidding documents (technical aspects). After the project activities have completed the procurement procedures required by the World Bank, and during the implementation of sub-project contracts, assist the PMO in strengthening contract management and acceptance work.

4. Project Monitoring and Evaluation

In accordance with the project results framework indicators specified in the project assessment documents, regularly conduct surveys on project monitoring indicator data, draft annual monitoring and evaluation reports, and assist the PMO in explaining issues related to the survey methodology and data reliability of the monitoring and evaluation data to the World Bank.

5. Informatization Management Consulting

Provide consulting services and technical guidance for the construction of informatization platforms in this project, including the "Scan-to-Trace" full-chain traceability platform for food, the "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" system, and the emergency real-time dispatch and command system. Services include assisting in the preparation and review of technical proposals, helping to resolve technical issues encountered during the procurement of information platforms, supervising the platform supervision work, assisting in the acceptance of informatization platforms, and providing professional technical guidance regarding the design, implementation, operation, and promotion of these platforms.

6. Translation Services

Based on project management needs, the service provider shall handle the translation of emails exchanged with the World Bank, World Bank memos, and various reports submitted to the World Bank. The original formats, such as PDF, Word, and Excel, must be preserved. Terminology must comply with industry or World Bank standards. The translation shall meet localization and proofreading requirements, adapt to the World Bank's official terminology database, and undergo multiple rounds of review to ensure compliance with World Bank document specifications.

7. On-site Services

The service provider shall participate in the daily management of the World Bank project throughout the entire process. The main responsibilities include daily liaison and coordination with the World Bank and relevant competent authorities; assisting in drafting work plans, procurement plans, and various progress reports; cooperating in completing the drafting of Terms of Reference (TOR), bid reviews, informatization platform acceptance, and monitoring and evaluation data collection; and undertaking tasks such as file archiving, daily translation, and meeting organization. The West African Power Pool (WAPP) was created by the highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the Conference of Heads of State and Government of the Member States held in Lomé, in December 1999. The Headquarters of the WAPP Secretariat is in Abomey-Calavi, Republic of Benin.

The ECOWAS strategic objective being implemented by the West African Power Pool (WAPP) is based on a dynamic vision of integrating national power grids into a unified regional electricity market, so that such a mechanism would, over the medium and long term, ensure to the ECOWAS citizens access to adequate power quality at an affordable price, and enhance the economic development of the Member States including industrialization growth, Health and Education improvement, Poverty Reduction, various Employment Opportunities Creation, etc…

To achieve its vision of operationalizing a unified ECOWAS regional electricity market, the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre (WAPP ICC), a Department within the WAPP Secretariat has been designated to perform the functions of a System Market Operator (SMO) responsible for coordinating the reliability of the WAPP Interconnected Transmission System (WAPPITS) made up of the power systems of fourteen (14) ECOWAS Member Countries and administration of the regional electricity market.

To this end, the WAPP Secretariat with the support of the World Bank within the Project “WAPP Côte d’Ivoire Interconnection and operationalization of the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market” intends to reinforce staffing of the ICC Department by filling a key vacant position, that of a Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

The Engineer will be selected competitively, and the successful candidates will be joining the current team in the Information and Coordination Centre (ICC) as it prepares to operationalize the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market.

Under the supervision of the Head of the System Operations Coordination Division, the Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer is responsible for the management of the ICC's Power System Database. He/She extracts data from various sources (APIs, HIVE tables, and other structured and unstructured data sources) to process and store large volumes of data, ensuring their accuracy, consistency and security. He/She develops reporting dashboards and analytical tools to support the analysis of power system operations, and supports the design, testing and implementation of models and databases for all systems requiring the WAPP Network Model.

The successful candidate shall be offered an initial Consultancy Contract of approximatively 17 months from the beginning of the assignment ( i.e.until April 30, 2028). Upon completion of the World Bank funding, the position shall be absorbed by WAPP.

The beginning of the assignment is planned for November 2026

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) ASSUMANT LA FONCTION DE SPECIALISTE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT AU SEIN DU PROGRAMME DE DEVELOPPEMENT INGA 3 (PDI3)

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : 7816-ZR (A) & 7815-ZR (B)

N° de référence de l’Avis : ZR-ADEPI-520117-CS-INDV

Date de Publication : le 10 septembre 2026

1. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie de réduction du déficit énergétique au niveau national, le Gouvernement de la RDC a demandé et obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) deux lignes de crédit (A et B) pour financer le « Programme de Développement du Projet INGA 3 (PDI 3) », et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit en vue d’effectuer des paiements au titre d’un contrat pour les prestations des services d’un(e) « Consultant assumant la fonction de Spécialiste de l'environnement au sein du Programme de Développement Inga 3 (PDI3)».

 

2. Au titre des services, sous l’autorité du Directeur de Projet, le/la Spécialiste Senior en Environnement aura pour mission d’assurer, pour le compte de l’ADPI-RDC au sein de l’ECP-PDI3, la prise en charge adéquate, efficace et traçable des aspects environnementaux de toutes les activités du Projet, conformément à la législation nationale applicable, au Cadre environnemental et social de la Banque mondiale, à l’Accord de financement, au Manuel d’Exécution du Projet (MEP), au Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social (PEES) et aux instruments environnementaux et sociaux du PDI3.

 

De manière spécifique, le (la) Consultant(e) aura comme responsabilité, entre autres de :

  • conseiller le Directeur de Projet, les équipes de l’ECP-PDI3 et de l’ADPI-RDC sur les questions sectorielles ainsi que sur la gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux liés au Projet ;
  • intégrer les exigences environnementales dans le Plan de Travail et Budget Annuel (PTBA), le Plan de Passation des Marchés (PPM), les Termes de Référence (TDR), les Dossiers d’Appel d’Offres (DAO), les contrats, les plans de travail, les livrables et les rapports des consultants et prestataires recrutés par le Projet ;
  • organiser ou appuyer le screening environnemental des activités et sous-projets et déterminer les instruments environnementaux requis ;
  • assurer la revue qualité et le suivi de la mise en œuvre des instruments environnementaux préparés par les consultants ;
  • contribuer à la préparation et au suivi des TDR des études environnementales et sociales, notamment les études environnementales et sociales stratégiques, les études d’impact cumulatif, les études d’impact environnemental et social (EIES), les Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES), les plans de gestion spécifiques et les TDR d’assistance technique ;
  • vérifier l’intégration des clauses environnementales, sociales, d’hygiène et de sécurité (ESHS), des codes de conduite, des exigences de santé et sécurité au travail (SST) et des mesures de gestion environnementale dans les marchés ;
  • contribuer, lorsque sollicité par l’ECP-PDI3, à l’évaluation technique des offres sur les aspects environnementaux, sans se substituer aux commissions compétentes ;
  • suivre l’exécution des mesures environnementales prévues dans le PEES, le Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (CGES), les PGES et les autres instruments spécifiques ;
  • réaliser ou appuyer les missions de surveillance et de suivi environnemental sur les sites d’études, de travaux, de réhabilitations, de routes rurales, de zones d’emprunt, de corridors ou d’installations temporaires ;
  • examiner les rapports environnementaux des consultants, entreprises et missions de contrôle et assurer le suivi de la clôture des commentaires, réserves et non-conformités ;
  • suivre les non-conformités, incidents, accidents, plaintes environnementales, mesures correctives et rapports des prestataires ;
  • notifier immédiatement au Directeur de Projet tout incident ou accident environnemental, de SST ou communautaire significatif et contribuer à la préparation des rapports requis ;
  • appuyer la formation des équipes du Projet, des prestataires et des parties prenantes sur les exigences environnementales, la SST, la gestion de la pollution et des déchets, la biodiversité et les clauses ESHS ;
  • veiller à l’appropriation des instruments environnementaux et sociaux par les équipes de l’ADPI-RDC et de l’ECP-PDI3, l’Unité Provinciale d’Appui (UPA), les prestataires et les bénéficiaires institutionnels ;

Le poste sera basé à Kinshasa, au sein de l’ECP-PDI3, avec des missions régulières à Matadi, dans les territoires ciblés du Kongo Central, sur le site d’Inga et dans toute autre zone pertinente pour les activités du PDI3.   • être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 minimum en sciences de l’environnement, gestion environnementale, biologie, écologie, agronomie, ingénierie, génie de l’environnement, ressources naturelles ou dans une discipline équivalente ;

  • justifier d’une expérience dans la réalisation de missions similaires financées par la Banque mondiale ou une autre institution financière internationale ;
  • disposer d’une bonne connaissance de la gestion des risques liés notamment à la SST, à la pollution, aux déchets, à la biodiversité, aux ressources en eau, au trafic, aux chantiers et aux incidents ;
  • disposer d’excellentes capacités d’analyse, de rédaction, de synthèse, de communication, de coordination et de travail en équipe ;
  • avoir une maîtrise du français écrit et parlé ; la maîtrise de l’anglais professionnel et la connaissance des langues nationales constituent des atouts.

Integrated Aquatic and Terrestrial Biodiversity Study on Naryn River (Kambarata-1 HPP)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA Credit 7601-KG / Grant TF-C4773-KG
Assignment Title: Integrated Aquatic and Terrestrial Biodiversity Study on Naryn River (Kambarata-1 HPP)
Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): KG/KA1/CS/2026/QCBS-04


The Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Technical Assistance for Kambarata 1 Hydropower Plant Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
The consulting services (“the Services”) include Integrated Aquatic and Terrestrial Biodiversity Study on Naryn River (Kambarata-1 HPP).
The objectives of this assignment are to:

1. Detailed biodiversity surveys/assessments for the construction of the diversion tunnel, expected to start in summer 2027. This includes research on:

(i) Baseline biodiversity studies of terrestrial ecosystems through systematic surveys of flora and fauna in activity impact zones (tunnel entrances, access roads, waste disposal sites, construction sites);

(ii) Development of measures to compensate and reimburse damage to biodiversity in the event of significant negative impacts being identified in the bypass tunnel section;

(iii) Identification and mapping of critical habitats and priority biodiversity sites within the bypass tunnel area.

(iv) Analysis of construction activities and their impact on biodiversity.

2. Closing biodiversity gaps identified in the ESIA. This includes research on:

(i) Aquatic Biodiversity (eDNA). Environmental DNA study is designed to establish a comprehensive biodiversity baseline using state-of-the-art environmental DNA (eDNA) methods and observational methods for aquatic ecosystems and traditional survey methods for terrestrial ecosystems, explicitly linked to: construction impact pathways and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) sub-plans for the construction of these diversion tunnels and the Cumulative Impact Assessment (CIA) for the project, supplementing the draft ESIA already prepared by the Kyrgyz Republic and disclosed on their website and that of the World Bank;

(ii) Terrestrial Biodiversity (Terrestrial Fauna and Flora). This study shall be carried out on the basis of the comments of the Ministry of Natural Resources No. 12-4/7302 of August 27, 2025 to address gaps in the ESIA and ESMP.

(iii) Impact Pathways. This study shall be carried out on the basis of the comments of the Ministry of Natural Resources No. 12-4/7302 of August 27, 2025 to address gaps in the ESIA and ESMP.

(iv)Critical Habitat. This study shall be carried out on the basis of the comments of the Ministry of Natural Resources No. 12-4/7302 of August 27, 2025 to address gaps in the ESIA and ESMP.

(v) Integration of study results into the ESIA and ESMP and other subplans.


The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest and can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YkEdvo1gU7lkYJxVGYGDNX-2eQGmlwHA/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106640225351494746259&rtpof=true&sd=true

The PMO under the Ministry of Energy of the Kyrgyz Republic now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”), which may form a consortium of associated firms, to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • Strong knowledge and experience in implementing the World Bank ESF, the World Bank Group's Environment, Health, and Safety (EHSG) General Guidelines, and/or other international financial institutions, as well as international industry best practices.
  • Experience with biodiversity offsets. Experience with transboundary environmental impacts and cumulative impact assessments.
  • At least seven years of experience in application of rigorous quality assurance/quality control protocols (QA/QC protocols) for field sampling, laboratory work, and data analysis.
  • Experience developing ESIA and ESMP projects.
  • Experience of work in similar ecosystems or in similar regions with knowledge of local fish species. Experience in Central Asia will be an advantage.
  • Proven experience in eDNA sampling, laboratory analysis, and bioinformatics for aquatic environments.
  • Experience of work with genetic databases (e.g., NCBI, BOLD) and tools for primer design and validation (e.g., ecoPCR).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications (type of association shall be clearly indicated in the proposal). DATE OF ISSUE: 10th September 2026

 

 

Background

 

The SADC Secretariat through the SADC Regional Statistics Project has received a grant.   1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
    1. Partner country

The Southern African Development Community (SADC).

 

    1. Contract authority

The Contracting Authority is SADC Secretariat, represented by its Executive Secretary.

 

    1. Background

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a Regional Economic Community comprising 16 Member States, namely; Angola, Botswana, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Established in 1992, SADC is committed to Regional Integration and poverty eradication within Southern Africa through economic development and ensuring peace and security.

 

Article 14 of the SADC Treaty establishes the SADC Secretariat as the principal executive institution of SADC. The Secretariat performs its mandate and functions within the policy, strategic and programme provisions outlined in the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) and the Vision 2050. The SADC Vision 2050 earmarks Statistics a priority cross-cutting sector whereby by 2050, the region strategic objective in statistics is to realize a robust and responsive regional statistical system to underpin regional integration processes, including measurement of progress and impact.

 

    1. Current situation in the sector

In the discipline of Official Statistics there is an absolute necessity of evolving towards programming languages oriented to modern data science to face new challenges such as fast prototyping innovative ideas, standardizing production processes and automatizing manual tasks. The implementation of statistical techniques, methods and methodologies can be done with Python functions and scripts in a more efficient way.


The Secretariat is prioritizing statistical capacity building as part of its implementation plan guided by the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) 2020-30. With the Regional Statistics Project funded by the World Bank, capacity building shall basically come in the form of development of practical guidelines in specific domains; rolling out national and regional training programmes and; assisting Member States through technical assistance. Data management and processing is within the sub-component 1.1 on improving capacity for data production, management and dissemination of the World Bank project.

 

With the growing need of analysing voluminous and complex survey data on a timely basis, open-source statistical softwares play a significant role. Thus, Secretariat is recruiting a consultancy firm which may include but not limited to research centres or universities to train SADC Member States statisticians on Python for beginners and intermediate level.

 

    1. Needs assessment

Member States were also requesting training on Python for official statisticians involved or not in Big Data and Data Science activities having no specific knowledge on the subject.

 

 

  1. OBJECTIVES, PURPOSE AND EXPECTED RESULTS
    1. Overall objective

The overall objective of this exercise is to train Member States on the use of statistical software for management of large database and analysis of complex surveys.

    1. Specific objectives (Purpose)

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake a national training on Python  for processing of data for official statistics, especially:

  1. to introduce participants to the Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write basic Python programs for data processing, analysis and visualization; and

 

  1. to provide participants with intermediate level knowledge on Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write Python programs for official statistics.

 

    1. Results to be achieved by the Consultancy Firm

The Consultancy Firm is expected to achieve the following result:

  1. Python component: Strengthened technical capacity of Statisticians from National Statistics Offices to have a good understanding of Python language and its ecosystem for use for Official Statistics purposes and to be familiar with syntax of Python for reading of a file, processing of data, modelling, aggregation and visualization.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK FOR TRAINING ON PYTHON
    1. Scope of work

The selected service provider is expected to deliver in-person technical training workshop on Python to process and analyze official statistics for data producers of official statistics at national level for respective Member State for 10 working days (5 working days for Beginners and 5 working days for intermediate levels)

The training includes theoretical and practical sessions to help participants understand Python syntax and its ecosystem for data management, statistical analysis, tabulations, graphics, and maps from complex census, survey data, and big data. The training report should contain summary of topics covered during training week. Training materials should also be shared to all participants and annexed to be training report

It is expected that the training to be done with real anonymized data obtained from censuses, survey and administrative data undertaken by National Statistics Offices.

 

    1. Geographical area to be covered

The assignment will be carried out in 10 selected Member States of SADC Region, namely (Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, Zimbabwe).

    1. Target groups

This consultancy is expected to target the National Statistics Office and other stakeholders, in particular, statisticians involved in processing and analysis of official statistics, large data and complex surveys.

    1. Specific work

The assignment will be carried out primarily through a national training in five selected Member States of SADC Region.

In particular, the consultant will be required to:

  1. Inception report detailing approach, methods, assumptions, risks, timelines and content of topics covered and training programme
  2. Develop a generic training materials to cater for practical training on Python.
  3. To tailor the programme to the needs of each Member State for intermediate level.
  4. To deliver the training at mutually agreed dates
  5. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for beginners’ level:
  • Essentials of Python environment and knowledge about the individual aspects of data processing pipeline (reading file, processing data, saving results, modelling, aggregation, visualization and saving results)
  • Essential syntax of Python; functions, main data structures (tuples, lists, dictionaries)
  • Importing data in Python
  • Creating, manipulating and converting common data structures
  • Merging data from different data sources or different questionnaires
  • Writing functions and using pre-existing functions
  • Introduction to the NumPy library
  • Creation and handling of arrays
  • Packages like Pandas, Matpotlib, Seaborn, Scikit-learn, Geopandas,

 

  1. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for intermediate level:

 

  • Performance and differences with respect to Python lists
  • Object-oriented programming
  • Mathematical operations and broadcasting
  • Use of Encapsulation with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Use of Inheritance with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Usage of universal functions (ufuncs)
  • Polymorphism applied to official statistics
  • Python and production of official statistics
  • Sampling and weighting with Python
  • Statistical models with Python
  • Python and processing of big data
  • Python and satellite image/GIS
  • Python and automation/machine learning

 

 

  1. Produce well documented Training Materials to be shared with participants with step-by-step indication for all the topics covered
  2. Produce a Training Report for each Member State with a summary of topics covered during the training and recommendations for implementation
  3. To do a pre- and Post-Training Surveys assessment of participants knowledge and identifying areas of improvement

The experts from the Firm shall assist participants in first handling of Python on the first day of the training for them to use it correctly.

The assignment is for training in 10 SADC Member States. The Firm shall be subject to evaluation after each training in a Member State. Continuation of contract is upon satisfactory completion and quality of the previous assignment.

In the discipline of Official Statistics there is an absolute necessity of evolving towards programming languages oriented to modern data science to face new challenges such as fast prototyping innovative ideas, standardizing production processes and automatizing manual tasks. The implementation of statistical techniques, methods and methodologies can be done with R functions, scripts and packages in a proper manner following the principles of modularity.


Secretariat is prioritizing statistical capacity building as part of its implementation plan guided by the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) 2020-30.
