Annex. E&S Screening, Risk Classification, and E&S Assessment and Management

 

E&S Screening and Risk Classification

As part of the project identification and prioritization process, the Consultant shall conduct an Environmental and Social (E&S) screening of all assets and sub-projects identified for potential inclusion under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. The purpose of this screening is to identify, at an early stage, the nature and significance of potential environmental and social risks and impacts associated with each sub-project, and to classify them accordingly to inform prioritization and downstream assessment requirements under Task 5.

The E&S screening shall be carried out in accordance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and shall include the following activities:

(a) Screening Checklist Development. The Consultant shall develop a standardized E&S screening checklist, to be reviewed and approved by EFL and the World Bank, covering the following parameters for each sub-project or asset replacement activity:

  • Nature, scale, and location of the proposed asset replacement works (e.g., generation assets, transmission and distribution infrastructure, substations, switchboards, transformers, and hydropower plant components);
  • Proximity to environmentally sensitive areas, including watercourses, riparian zones, protected areas, forests, and ecologically significant habitats;
  • Proximity to communities, settlements, sacred sites, and areas of cultural heritage significance;
  • Land access requirements, including temporary or permanent land acquisition, easements, or restrictions on land use;
  • Potential for generation of hazardous waste, including oils, asbestos-containing materials (ACM), SF6 gas, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), and other legacy contaminants associated with aging electrical infrastructure;
  • Potential for impacts on labor and working conditions, occupational health and safety, and community health and safety during works; and
  • Potential for disproportionate impacts on vulnerable or marginalized groups, including women, youth, and indigenous communities.

(b) Application of the Screening Checklist. The Consultant shall apply the approved screening checklist to each sub-project or asset cluster identified in Task 4, drawing on available data, site reconnaissance findings, and stakeholder inputs gathered under Task 2. For hydropower-related asset replacements, the screening shall additionally assess:

  • The potential for works to alter water release regimes, turbine operations, or intake structures in ways that may affect downstream river flows, including environmental flows (eflows);
  • Potential impacts on aquatic ecosystems, freshwater biodiversity, and ecosystem services dependent on river flows; and
  • Any associated civil works within or adjacent to river corridors, including intake structures, penstocks, tailraces, and powerhouses.

(c) E&S Risk Classification. Based on the screening outcomes, the Consultant shall assign each sub-project or asset replacement activity a preliminary E&S risk classification consistent with the World Bank ESF risk categories (High, Substantial, Moderate, or Low). The classification shall consider both the type and scale of potential impacts and the sensitivity of the receiving environment and social context.

(d) Screening Report. The Consultant shall prepare an E&S Screening Report summarizing the results of the screening exercise for all sub-projects. The report shall include, for each sub-project: the completed screening checklist, the preliminary E&S risk classification, the rationale for the classification, and recommended E&S assessment and management measures required under Task 5. The Screening Report shall form an input to the Project Identification deliverable and shall be shared with EFL, the Ministry of Finance, and the World Bank for review and clearance prior to finalization.

The outcomes of the E&S screening shall directly inform the selection and sequencing of sub-projects for the first batch of implementation, ensuring that sub-projects with manageable E&S risks are prioritized, and that appropriate assessment and management measures are in place before procurement commences.

 

 

Environmental and Social Assessment and Management

Building on the E&S screening conducted under Task 4, the Consultant shall undertake Environmental and Social (E&S) assessments and prepare the corresponding management instruments for the sub-projects identified for the implementation under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. All assessments and instruments shall comply with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable national environmental legislation of Fiji (including the Environment Management Act 2005 and associated regulations), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP).

    1. Scope and Approach

The E&S assessment shall cover all sub-projects in the first batch, as identified and screened under Task 4, including but not limited to:

  • Replacement of aged switchboards, transformers, and associated substation equipment across EFL's network;
  • Rehabilitation or replacement of generation assets at EFL's hydropower stations as identified under in the main text; and
  • Any associated civil, structural, or access works.

The scale and depth of assessment shall be proportionate to the E&S risk classification assigned to each sub-project under Task 4.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Assessment — Hydropower Asset Replacement

For asset replacement activities at hydropower stations, the Consultant shall prepare a standalone E&S assessment addressing the specific environmental and social sensitivities associated with hydropower infrastructure. The ESIA shall be prepared by qualified environmental and social specialists and shall include, at minimum, the following components:

 

(a) Description of the Existing Environment and Baseline Conditions

The Consultant shall compile and, where necessary, supplement existing baseline data to characterize the environmental and social baseline for each hydropower site and its area of influence, including:

  • Hydrology and water resources: river flow regimes, seasonal variability, historical discharge data, and existing water abstractions or diversions;
  • Aquatic ecology: species composition, abundance, and distribution of freshwater fish, macroinvertebrates, and other aquatic biota in rivers upstream and downstream of each facility;
  • Riparian and terrestrial ecology: vegetation communities, wildlife habitats, and any protected or endemic species in the project area;
  • Water quality: existing water quality conditions in receiving waterbodies;
  • Ecosystem services: identification and characterization of ecosystem services provided by river systems and dependent on flow regimes, including provisioning services (fisheries, water supply for downstream communities and agriculture), regulating services (flood attenuation, water purification), and cultural services (recreational, spiritual, and cultural values associated with rivers); and
  • Social baseline: communities and livelihoods dependent on river resources downstream of each facility, including subsistence fishing, smallholder irrigation, and cultural or ceremonial uses of water.

 

(b) Environmental Flow (E-Flow) Assessment

Given the small scale of the hydropower facility, the Consultant shall conduct a proportionate desktop E-flow review rather than a full E-flow assessment study. The review shall be commensurate with the nature of the asset replacement works and the associated level of hydrological risk.

The desktop review shall:

  • Document the existing operational flow regime at the facility, including any minimum flow release requirements specified in the facility's existing operating licence, consent conditions, or EFL operational procedures;
  • Confirm whether the proposed asset replacement works involve any physical changes to the intake structure, diversion weir, penstock, or tailrace that could alter the volume, timing, or continuity of water diverted or released — and if no such changes are proposed, note this explicitly as a basis for scoping out a detailed E-flow assessment;
  • Apply a simple hydrological desktop method — such as the Tennant (Montana) Method using available mean annual flow data — to provide a reference check on whether existing minimum flow releases at the facility are broadly consistent with accepted thresholds for maintaining basic ecological functions in the downstream river reach; and
  • Based on the above, conclude either that: (i) existing minimum flow provisions are adequate and no additional E-flow measures are required; or (ii) a gap exists that warrants a specific operational protocol or condition to be incorporated into the ESMP.

 

(c) Impact Assessment

The Consultant shall identify, predict, and evaluate the significance of potential environmental and social impacts associated with hydropower asset replacement works, covering both the construction and operational phases. Key impact pathways to be assessed shall include:

  • Changes to downstream flow regimes during works (e.g., dewatering, cofferdam installation, temporary flow diversion) and their effects on aquatic habitats, species, and ecosystem services;
  • Alteration of sediment transport and geomorphic processes resulting from changes to turbine operation or intake structures;
  • Impacts on aquatic biodiversity, particularly fish passage and migration, arising from works at intake or tailrace structures;
  • Risks of water quality degradation from construction activities, including turbidity, sedimentation, and potential release of oils, lubricants, or hazardous materials;
  • Hazardous waste generation and management, including oils, asbestos-containing materials, PCBs, SF6 gas, and other materials associated with aged electrical and mechanical equipment;
  • Community health and safety risks
  • Impacts on downstream communities dependent on river-based livelihoods and ecosystem services.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs)

The Consultant shall prepare ESMPs for each sub-project in the first batch, integrating findings from the E&S assessment (for hydropower facilities) and the E&S screening assessments. The ESMPs shall:

  • Describe, for each identified impact, the proposed hierarchy of mitigation measures (avoidance, minimization, mitigation, and compensation or offset where residual impacts remain);
  • Include specific management measures for: hazardous waste handling and disposal (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6); erosion and sediment control during civil works; hydropower operational protocols to maintain E-flows during construction phases; worker health and safety; community health and safety;
  • Specify monitoring requirements, including parameters to be monitored, monitoring locations, frequency, responsible parties, and reporting arrangements, with particular attention to downstream aquatic ecology and water quality monitoring at hydropower sites;
  • Define institutional responsibilities for ESMP implementation, supervision, and reporting within EFL;
  • Include a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) consistent with World Bank ESF requirements, covering all project-affected communities; and
  • Include an estimated budget for ESMP implementation.

 

    1. Stakeholder Engagement and Disclosure

In coordination with Task 2, the Consultant shall support EFL in conducting targeted stakeholder consultations on the E&S assessment and ESMP findings for each sub-project. Consultations shall be conducted in accordance with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan developed under Task 2, and shall be culturally appropriate and accessible to women, indigenous communities, and other vulnerable groups. Consultation records, including attendance, issues raised, and responses, shall be documented and appended to the ESIA and ESMP.

 

    1. Integration of E&S Requirements into Bidding Documents

The Consultant shall work closely with the procurement specialist engaged for Task 6 to ensure that all relevant E&S requirements are systematically integrated into the bidding documents for the asset replacement sub-projects. This shall include:

(a) E&S Specifications and Requirements. The Consultant shall prepare an Environmental and Social Requirements (ESR) section to be included within the bidding documents for each contract package, covering: Contractor obligations with respect to ESMP implementation, including preparation and submission of a Contractor Environmental and Social Management Plan (C-ESMP) prior to commencement of works; specific technical requirements for hazardous waste management (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6, and other hazardous materials from aged equipment), including approved disposal or recycling methods, handling procedures, and documentation requirements;

(b) E&S Performance Standards in Contract Conditions. The Consultant shall recommend appropriate contract conditions and performance standards to ensure contractor compliance with E&S requirements, including provisions for: submission and approval of the C-ESMP as a condition precedent to commencement of works; regular E&S reporting by the contractor;  and consequences for non-compliance, including stop-work orders and financial remedies.

(c) E&S Rated Criteria. The Consultant shall recommend criteria for evaluating contractor E&S capacity and performance as part of the qualification and evaluation criteria for each bidding package, covering contractor experience with E&S management on similar infrastructure projects, availability of qualified E&S personnel, and approach to hazardous materials management.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL (E&S) SPECIALIST

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) - Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)

1. Introduction and Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499), a World Bank-supported initiative estimated at USD 230 million. The project aims to accelerate renewable-energy development, modernize the power grid, rehabilitate aging infrastructure, and reform the power sector to attract private investment in solar energy. Key interventions span Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni, including solar PV/BESS parks of more than 50 MW each, grid-evacuation infrastructure, transmission-line upgrades and modernization of existing power stations.

The Initial Environmental and Social Review Summary has classified the project's environmental and social risks as Substantial, reflecting biodiversity impacts, customary iTaukei land tenure, community health and safety, labor influx, SEA/SH risks, and supply-chain concerns associated with PV modules and battery energy storage systems.

EFL is establishing a Project Preparation Unit (PPU) to prepare the project for appraisal and Board approval. The E&S Specialist will lead preparation of required E&S instruments, integrate E&S requirements into technical and procurement outputs, and prepare the TOR for a separate capacity-building assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The objective is to ensure that GFPP-financed preparation activities and the investments they support comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, applicable Fiji law, and Good International Industry Practice.

3. Scope of Work

The Consultant will perform the following tasks, organized into five functional areas:

3.1 General E&S Support to the PPU

• Serve as the PPU's E&S focal point and advise the Project Manager and technical teams on application of the ESF.

• Screen preparation activities and concept designs, identify applicable standards and instruments, and maintain an E&S Risk Register with actions, responsibilities and status.

• Prepare ESCP inputs, TORs for specialized studies, and E&S requirements for technical specifications and bidding documents; oversee related consultant outputs.

• Provide practical ESF training and on-the-job support to the PPU and relevant EFL staff.

• Coordinate with the World Bank, relevant Fiji agencies, TLTB, technical consultants and EFL departments, and maintain records of key decisions and actions.

3.2 Preparation of E&S Instruments Required by Appraisal

This is the most critical function of the assignment. The E&S Specialist will prepare the following appraisal-stage instruments and related outputs:

a. E&S Scoping Studies with Critical Habitat Screening

• Lead scoping studies for solar PV/BESS parks on Vanua Levu and Taveuni, grid-evacuation infrastructure, and new or upgraded transmission lines.

• Conduct structured Critical Habitat screening under ESS6 using available biodiversity data, including IUCN Red List species, Fiji endemic avifauna information, and protected-area registries.

• Where critical habitat is identified or cannot be ruled out, prepare detailed assessments and, where necessary, a Biodiversity Management Plan with offset strategies, no-go zones and seasonal restrictions.

• Include baseline social surveys, land-tenure mapping, community presence, vulnerable-group identification, and climate-resilience considerations such as cyclone, flooding and sea-level-rise risks.

b. Environmental and Social Management Plan - Aging Asset Replacement

• Prepare a site-specific ESMP for rehabilitation and replacement of aging power infrastructure under Component 3, covering baseline conditions, construction and operational risks, hazardous materials including PCBs, asbestos and e-waste, mitigation, monitoring, emergency response, contractor requirements, responsibilities, schedules and costs.

c. Resettlement Policy Framework

• Prepare an RPF consistent with ESS5 covering legal and institutional arrangements and gap analysis; eligibility and cut-off dates; entitlements and replacement-cost valuation; livelihood restoration; procedures for site-specific plans; consultation and grievance arrangements; monitoring, responsibilities and budget provisions.

d. Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report

(I) Scope of Service

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;

(II) Service Contents

1. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services

Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

2. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

The Ministry of Water and Irrigation has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank), the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and Global Concessional Financing Facility (GCFF) in the amount of US$300,000,000 to be managed by the World Bank, toward the cost of the Jordan Water Sector Efficiency Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services to be procured under this project.

The World Bank funded project will have the following components:

  • Component 1: Sustainable Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Reduction
  • Component 2: Increased energy efficiency and reduced energy supply costs
  • Component 3: Water security measures to underpin efficiency improvements
  • Component 4: Institutional strengthening for water sector Efficiency
  • Component 5: Contingency Emergency Response

 

The assignment is proposed under Component 1 of the project –NRW.

The consulting services (“the Services”) is

to design in detail and prepare for implementation a comprehensive Zarqa Governorate SCADA system, in order to accomplish the following objectives for the Zarqa Governorate Water Systems:

1.            Monitor the quality and quantity of the water supplied from the resources.

2.            Control and manage the water resources to conveniently feed the main and terminal reservoirs.

3.            Monitor and control the quality and quantity of the water in the distribution reservoirs, distribution network and all water facilities.

4.            Optimize the operation and maintenance, and energy costs of all the water system.

5.            Monitor and control the water facilities by detecting the emergency faults (alarms) and deal with these faults with minimum reaction fixing time.

6.            Ensure the water quality by installing on site chlorine analysis on the primary and secondary networks.

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

IV. DELIVERABLES

The Consultant shall deliver the following key deliverables during the implementation of the Assignment.

Deliverable 1. Inception Report

Within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date of the Contract, the Consultant shall submit a Draft Inception Report, including:

  • work plan and timeline;
  • expert mobilisation plan;
  • risk assessment and mitigation measures;
  • Quality Assurance Plan.

Deliverable 2. Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 20 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

 

Deliverable 3. Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 21 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

Deliverable 4. Final Completion Report

The following outputs shall be delivered under this deliverable and documented in the Final Completion Report:

  • full package with forty-one (41) final approved programs;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities;
  • lessons learned and next steps for further implementation.

The Consultant shall submit a Draft Final Completion Report no later than one month before the completion of the Assignment, summarising overall implementation results, achievement of objectives and targets, key lessons learned, and recommendations for further institutionalisation and sustainability.

Reports Submission and Acceptance Procedure

The following procedure shall apply to all reports submitted under this Assignment: the Inception Report (Deliverable 1), Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 2), and Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 3) and the Final Completion Report (Deliverable 4).

The exact format of the reports will be discussed and agreed upon with MoES and, where applicable, with the World Bank, upon contract signing and before the commencement of the Assignment. All reports and deliverables will be submitted in a minimum of two (2) hard copies in English and two (2) hard copies in Ukrainian. The products developed (model programs as well as methodological materials for development for Ukrainian-speaking users) shall be submitted in Ukrainian only, without translation, and included as annexes to the relevant reports. All materials developed under this Assignment shall become the property of MoES.

The Consultant shall submit:

  • the draft version of the Inception Report – within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs  – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of the Final Report – at latest 30 calendar days before the completion of the services.

The draft of each report shall be submitted in electronic (Word/Excel and PDF) format to the Client’s email address specified in the Contract. The Client will review the draft within 14 calendar days from the date of receipt and provide comments, or confirm the quality and correspondence of the Assignment with the requirements of these Terms of Reference. The Consultant, within 7 calendar days from receipt of comments, shall process them and submit the revised report in electronic and paper format, together with a table indicating, for each comment, the method of its consideration or justification for any deviation.

If the Client has no comments on the revised report, the report shall be deemed approved, which shall be confirmed by a signed Acceptance Certificate for Services. If the Client does not respond with comments within the above-mentioned period, the draft report shall be deemed accepted.

If required by MoES, the Consultant shall provide ad-hoc reports within 3–7 calendar days, depending on the complexity of the request.

V. REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Consultant

The Consultant must be a legally registered firm or a Joint Venture / Consortium of firms.

Minimum Qualification Requirements (Pass/Fail Basis)

Failure to meet any of the requirements below shall result in disqualification.

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 3 (three) years of experience in education, curriculum development, institutional development, or related fields;
  • At least 3 (three) successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:

–       curriculum development or educational program design;

–       vocational education or education sector projects;

–       capacity building programs for education institutions.

In case of a Joint Venture / Consortium (JVCA), the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least 3 (three) years of relevant experience and participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments. The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial Capacity

  • Average annual turnover for the last 3 completed financial years shall be at least USD 150,000 or equivalent.

 In case of a JVCA: Lead Member: minimum 50% of the annual turnover requirement; Other members: minimum 25% of the annual turnover requirement; Combined: must fully meet the annual turnover requirement. Audited financial statements or verified financial documents shall be provided.

Experience with Donor-Funded Projects

  • At least one assignment financed by international financial institutions or bilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, EU, GIZ, UNICEF, etc.) within the last 5 years is an advantage.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) PROGRAM

Grant number:    IDA-E0780

Job title: SRSEI Project Coordinator

Reference Number: MZ-PMU-561409-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve accountability for day-to-day implementation oversight of assigned PIU activities in the designated province(s), serving as the primary operational interface between field execution and the PCU. The PIU Coordinator will ensure that all components are effectively executed, and in a timely manner in accordance with the implementation plan.

The Project Coordinator will be required to work in close liaison with the PCU, ANE, INATRO and other stakeholders and in accordance with the Legal Agreements, and various approved project implementation manuals. A high degree of initiative and a pro-active and consultative approach will be required from the Project Coordinator in order to achieve the outcomes of this assignment. The expected duration of the assignment is 24 months. There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The Project Coordinator is required to report to the Portfolio Coordinator at the CPU of the MTL

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work; (ii) a cover letter, no more than two pages long, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The Project Coordinator should have the following minimum qualifications and skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field. 
  • At least Fifteen (15) years general working experience, of which least 10 years of progressive experience in civil works project management specifically for roads of at least 50 km or other infrastructure of similar complexity to the program
  • Experience in contract administration and management of consultants/contractors, including tracking deliverables, reviewing outputs, facilitating acceptance, and supporting invoice certification processes.
  • Experience  in contract management based on FIDIC, including prevention and/or mitigation of claims that involve financial losses to the Employer.
  • Knowledge of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), in particular ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, and ESS5..
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or coordinate teams and to work effectively with government counterparts at central and provincial levels, private sector, communities and other stakeholders.
  • Working experience in Mozambique.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken)

Desirable requirements

  • Master degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field.
  • Familiarity with OPBRC and/or Design Build contract structures.
  • Familiarity with the latest project management techniques and tools is essential. Having professional accreditation for Project Management from a recognized body.
  • Proven experience coordinating procurement processes and supporting preparation of TORs/specifications/bidding documents, and following procurement steps through contract award.
  • Demonstrated experience in GBV/SEA/SH-sensitive programme environments.
  • Good knowledge of BOQ interpretation, Detailing, Specifications, Public Procurement, Project/Contract management, Quality Control and dispute resolution.
  • Experience in the road safety standards.
  • Familiarity with national policies, procedures, and government processes.
  • Experience coordinating field implementation and undertaking regular site visits, including documenting progress, risks, quality and safeguards issues.
  • Familiarity with STEP (World Bank's procurement tracking platform) and experience with e-SISTAFE or equivalent government financial management systems.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in English must be sent in writing to the address below (only by e-mail) up to 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Background:  In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance. 

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually-reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.  MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative, under Component 1, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI) is strengthening its role in Advancing regional trade integration through Somalia’s accession to the East African Community (EAC) and the World Trade Organization (WTO).

 MoF intends to apply for part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the position of Industrial Development Advisor for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Industrial Development Advisor will support MoCI in implementing industrial policies, formalizing businesses, improving export readiness, developing Special Economic Zones, strengthening intellectual property administration, coordinating stakeholders, drafting regulatory instruments, delivering staff training, facilitating public–private dialogue, and preparing implementation plans and progress reports.

 

 

 

Responsibilities: an The Industrial Development Advisor will support the implementation of Somalia’s industrial policies by developing work plans, regulatory instruments, standards, incentive frameworks, and procedures. The Advisor will promote business formalization, export readiness, and access to EAC, AfCFTA, and WTO markets. The Advisor will provide technical support for Special Economic Zones, intellectual property administration, investment facilitation, value-chain development, and environmental compliance. The role will also strengthen coordination between MoCI, government institutions, and the private sector, with attention to micro, small, and women-owned industries. The Advisor will train MoCI and SEZ staff and support public–private consultations on industrial and trade barriers. The Advisor will also prepare regulatory frameworks, implementation plans, training materials, progress reports, and strategic advisory documents.

All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link: https://moci.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ToR-Industrial-Development-Advisor-2.pdf 

2.   Skills and qualifications

•   Master’s degree in industrial economics, Development Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

•    Minimum of 8 years of demonstrated experience in industrial development, investment facilitation, value chain development, or related regulatory reform work within government or international development contexts and supportive of business formalization and external trade.

•    Demonstrated knowledge of industrial policy design, business formalization and licensing systems, special economic zone governance, or productive sector development in sub-Saharan Africa or comparable fragile and conflict-affected settings.

•    Experience with intellectual property administration or quality and standards systems is an advantage.

•    Demonstrated ability to manage inter-ministerial coordination and facilitate multi-stakeholder consultation processes.

•    Experience with World Bank or international development projects is highly preferred.

•    Proficiency in English and excellent written and verbal communication skills are required. Fluency in Somali is an advantage.

Assignment Title: Consultancy services for Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia

Reference No. ZM-MOFNP-570604-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Irrigated and Sustainable Agriculture for Transformation (ISAT) Project Preparation and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  The Project Preparation Grant financing is intended to support the identification, technical assessment, and preparation of priority irrigation schemes that can be taken forward under the full ISAT operation.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia.

Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the design of a FLID component for the ISAT project, including the design and piloting of a Results-Based Financing framework tailored to FLID.

Scope of Work

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks:

a) Fast diagnostic (data collection, analysis): Understand the bottlenecks to scaling up FLID in Zambia and scoping for a Result Based Financing (RBF) framework around the identified irrigation schemes.

  • Characterize FLID potential at farm level (farm size, assets, affordability gaps)
  • Survey the current private sector landscape that is providing goods (supply of irrigation equipment) and services (irrigation services) to assess equipment capital and operational costs for the range of farmer types and farm sizes, understand private sector challenges and draw on private sector insights into opportunities for rapid irrigation technology uptake and expansion.
  • Understand the existing public financing structures and mechanisms for financing smallholder irrigation.
  • Explore the policy and legal barriers in the enabling environment constraining smallholder farmers in autonomously carrying out small-scale irrigation development.

b) FLID intervention and RBF Design: Translate the diagnostic into a set of feasible, scalable FLID intervention models.

  • Develop the design of potential FLID interventions within the ISAT project, providing different options and potential scenarios based on the diagnostic of farmers’ assets, willingness to pay, providers’ capacity, among others.
  • Design an RBF framework and its parameters: Key Result Indicators (KRIs), payment triggers/schedules, eligibility, verification, financial flows, subsidy/rebate, risk-sharing.

c) Piloting the Methodology: The pilot phase serves as a controlled environment to test the feasibility, scalability, and sustainability of the proposed FLID intervention. Particularly irrigation modernization, financing mechanisms, and private sector partnerships. The four sequential stages of the methodology include:

  • Elaborate a piloting methodology of the proposed interventions in Zambia accounting for the time constraint of the project preparation, outlining the process for selecting testing sites, testing financing mechanisms, partnering with irrigation equipment providers and any other intervention design aspects that might be piloted.
  • Identify 10 appropriate sites for piloting based on a set of pre-defined characteristics.
  • Onboard participants of the pilots such as providers, financial institutions, districts, farmers.
  • Define the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework to assess the pilot’s performance.

d) Pilot implementation and evaluation: Implement FLID interventions with continuous technical support, collect baseline, midline and end-line data, identify challenges along the implementation process to refine the model and document lessons for national scale-up. Specifically:

  • Deploy the FLID interventions and RBF mechanisms in the selected zones.
  • Execute the MEL framework.
  • Conduct a structured assessment of pilot outcomes and rank the best-performing options

Duration of the Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within seven (7) calendar months after signing of contract between November 2026 and May 2027.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Must be a legally registered firm with a minimum of 5 years of continuous operations in providing consultancy services.
  2. Experience in similar assignments, evidence of at least three similar assignments completed in Sub-Saharan Africa within the past ten years. Experience must include:
  • At least one assignment related to Farmer-Led Irrigation Development or smallholder irrigation systems
  • At least one assignment involving performance-based or results-based contracting.

      3. Proven track record working with government agencies, private sector actors, and                          development partners (Consultant to provide copies of contracts for past assignments or                completion certificates as evidence).

      4. The firm must demonstrate strong technical multidisciplinary expertise in Irrigation and                Water Resources Engineering, Agricultural Economics, Market Systems Development and            Private Sector Engagement and Environmental and Social Risk Management

      5.  Managerial capabilities indicating the general qualifications and experience of Principals               (key staff of the firm) and the structure of the organization.

The above required relevant qualifications and experience relate to the qualifications and experience of the firm and should not be based on individual experts as this is not required at this stage.

« TRANSFORME-RDC »

 

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

(SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS INDIVIDUELS)

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL POUR L’ELABORATION D’UN NOUVEAU PLAN QUINQUENNAL DE L’AGENCE NATIONALE DE DEVELOPPEMENT DE L'ENTREPRENEURIAT CONGOLAIS (ANADEC) INTEGRANT LA REDEVABILITE

 

 
  

 

N° de référence : ZR-TRANSFORME-566552-CS-INDV

Source de financement : Banque mondiale, Crédit n°7101-ZR / Don E0280-ZR

Date de publication : 16 septembre 2026

Date de clôture :  1er Octobre 2026

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et reçu un crédit et un don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) en vue de financer le coût du « Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et une mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC)» et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds de ce crédit et don pour les « Services d’un Consultant Individuel pour l’élaboration d’un nouveau plan quinquennal de l’Agence Nationale de Développement de l'Entrepreneuriat Congolais (ANADEC) intégrant la redevabilité ».

 

  1. Le présent avis d’appel public à manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 12 septembre 2022 ainsi que sur les sites de Mediacongo (www.mediacongo.net) et de PADMPME (www.padmpme.cd) respectivement le 13 et 14 septembre 2022 et paru dans le journal « La Prospérité n°5916 » le 14 septembre 2022.

 

  1. Les services sollicités consiste à doter l’ANADEC d’un nouveau plan quinquennal intégrant la redevabilité, comme étant un cadre stratégique de référence pour ses organes statutaires et opérationnels ainsi que pour les partenaires et  comprennent : (i) l’Élaboration d’un plan stratégique quinquennal clair, réaliste et aligné sur le périmètre d’intervention de l’ANADEC et les priorités du Gouvernement, (ii) le Renforcement des capacités de pilotage de l’ANADEC à travers un plan quinquennal orienté résultats, (iii) le Renforcement des capacités de l’ANADEC à élaborer leur propre plan quinquennal dans le futur à travers des outils opérationnels, (v) l’Intégration des principes de redevabilité dans les interventions et le fonctionnement de l’agence et (vi) la Proposition d’un dispositif de mise en œuvre et de suivi du plan.

 

  1. L’UCP-TRANSFORME invite les Candidats (Consultants Individuels) admissibles à manifester leurs intérêts pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants (Individuels) intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.  

 

  1. Le Consultant devra disposer du profil minimum suivant :

 

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de BAC+5 en sciences économiques, développement, management, gestion de projet, gestion des organisations, finance ou une discipline similaire ;
  • Être doté d’une expérience professionnelle confirmée de 10 à 15 ans sur des thématiques en lien avec l’entrepreneuriat, les politiques publiques de développement du secteur privé et les questions de planification stratégique et d’organisation des structures publiques ;
  • Avoir conduit avec succès au moins 5 missions similaires pour l’élaboration de plans quinquennaux pour une structure publique dont au moins 3 en Afrique Subsaharienne ;
  • Avoir des connaissances de l’écosystème entrepreneurial et de ses acteurs (trices) en RDC ;
  • Avoir la maîtrise du français.

 

  1. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025 ci-après désigné « Règlement de Passation des Marchés », qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels, telle que décrite dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025 en vertu du Nouveau Cadre de Passation des Marchés Publics (NCPM), et des « Lignes Directrices »  de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet.

 

  1. Les Consultants (Individuels) intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires, notamment sur les termes de référence, à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau suivantes : de 9 à 16 heures (heure locale, TU+1) ou sur le site web « www.transforme.cd ».

Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites, en langue française, doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous, par courrier physique ou électronique (e-mail), au plus tard le 1er Octobre 2026 à 16 heures (heure locale, TU +1) et porter clairement la mention ci-après : AMI N°ZR-TRANSFORME-566552-CS-INDV « Recrutement d’un Consultant Individuel pour l’élaboration d’un nouveau plan quinquennal de l’Agence Nationale de Développement de l'Entrepreneuriat Congolais (ANADEC) intégrant la redevabilité ».

Assignment Title: Employer’s Technical Supervision

Reference No: MN-MOE-ESP4-3-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of Mongolia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fourth Energy Sector Project (P509161) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will provide Employer’s Technical Supervision services for the design, construction, installation, testing, commissioning, handover, and Defects Notification Period of the Mandalgobi – Arvaikheer 220 kV transmission line and associated substation  works, to be implemented under multiple contract lots, in ensuring compliance with contractual requirements, applicable laws and legislation of Mongolia, and the World Bank Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), including relevant Quality standards and environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) standards. The Services shall cover all phases of the Project lifecycle.

The assignment duration shall be thirty-six (36) months, comprising approximately: (i) twenty-four (24) months for design review, construction supervision, testing and commissioning, and support to the Employer up to the issuance of the Taking-Over Certificate (TOC); and (ii) twelve (12) months of Defects Notification Period support on an oncall basis.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for assignment can be found at:

           https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dGjcHPrmfl4bQQEB4LlzhboAafIhPHlO/view?usp=sharing

The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (GoKP), through the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization (PEDO), is implementing the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Hydropower & Renewable Energy Development (KHRE) Program with financial assistance of the World Bank.

The objective of the Program is to support the development of hydropower and renewable energy resources in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, strengthen institutional capacity, and improve the operational, commercial, and governance frameworks of PEDO.

In this regard, PEDO intends to engage a qualified Consulting Firm as a Management Support Consultant (MSC) to provide institutional strengthening, strategic advisory, implementation support, and capacity development services.

The Consultant shall provide services including, but not limited to, the following areas:

  • Institutional review and organizational restructuring
  • Human Resource Management (HRM) framework development
  • Financial management, budgeting, and investment planning
  • Tariff, commercial, and regulatory advisory
  • Procurement and contract management strengthening
  • ERP and Project Monitoring Information System (PMIS) advisory
  • Legal and regulatory framework support
  • Capacity building, change management, and institutional reforms

The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing full-time technical advisory support to the implementation of Component 3 Enhanced Human Resource Capacity, Communications and Change Management of the PFM II Project, including:

  • Subcomponent 3.1: Human Resource Capacity Development, focusing on competency development, skills and training needs assessments, professional development and certification programmes, training partnerships, workforce development, knowledge retention, and institutional capacity strengthening; and
  • Subcomponent 3.2: Communications and Change Management, focusing on FMIS change management, organizational readiness, stakeholder communication, citizen engagement, communication of PFM reforms, and coordination of related transparency activities.

The Human Resource Development and Change Management Advisor will support the Government of FSM in operationalizing existing human resource development, capacity development, training, change management, FMIS adoption, stakeholder communication and citizen engagement strategies and frameworks developed under the Project.

The assignment will be based in Palikir, Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia, with travel to the four State Governments as required. The assignment is expected to be full-time for twenty-four (24) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

The Department of Finance and Administration now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.).

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. Minimum Master’s degree in Human Resource Management, Organizational Development, Public Administration, Change Management, Management, Education, or related field
  2. Minimum ten (10) years of professional experience in human resource development, organizational development, institutional strengthening, workforce development, or capacity development, preferably in the public sector.
  3. Minimum five (5) years of experience in change management, competency development, and capacity building/training in public financial management, public sector reform, or development projects;

 

Desirable :

  1. Experience in developing and implementing competency frameworks, training programmes, professional development and certification programmes;
  2. Experience in change management and organizational readiness for Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS) or other digital transformation initiatives;
  3. Demonstrated experience working with government institutions and stakeholders in multidisciplinary and multicultural environments;
  4. Experience working in Pacific island countries and/or similar remotely located Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
