August 2024 to September 30, 2030

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) for the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project. The project supports participating Pacific Island Countries to maintain continuous access to correspondent banking services and address payment, regulatory and financial integrity constraints that contribute to de-risking in the region.

Component 2, Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization, includes support for payment system oversight and regulation, national payment systems, regional harmonization and payments data. Related regional work includes the Pacific Payment Mechanism (PPM) feasibility study, which examines options for aggregating payment flows and improving economies of scale.

The National Reserve Bank of Tonga (NRBT) has requested support to recruit a National Payments Expert. NRBT has developed a five-year National Payment Services Strategy and is progressing its Payment Systems and Services Bill. The September 2026 concept note records that the Bill had passed its first reading in Parliament and was expected to return for further parliamentary consideration. The Expert will review the latest legislative position and implementation requirements with NRBT at inception.

The assignment will support implementation of the existing Strategy and strengthen NRBT's capacity to oversee and develop Tonga's payment system. The Expert will work alongside NRBT staff to turn strategic priorities into a sequenced work programme and support implementation, industry coordination and knowledge transfer.

 

Objective of the Position

The objective is to provide hands-on technical advisory and implementation support to NRBT in implementing its National Payment Services Strategy and improving the efficiency, resilience and oversight of Tonga's payment systems.

The Expert will support priority domestic initiatives and NRBT's active participation in the PPM feasibility study. The work will help NRBT identify the requirements for possible future participation in the PPM and prioritise preparatory actions, taking account of the study's findings, NRBT's mandate, available resources and national priorities.

 

Scope of Services

The Expert will provide country-level, time-based support on payment system matters. Activities and expected outputs will be agreed with NRBT, PIFS and the World Bank payments team through a 12-month work plan and updated through periodic work planning discussions.

  • i. Inception and work planning
  • Review the National Payment Services Strategy, the latest Payment Systems and Services Bill, existing implementation plans, payment infrastructure and projects, staffing arrangements and payments-related technical assistance. Review relevant CBR Project, CBR Roadmap and PPM materials supplied by PIFS and the World Bank.
  • Prepare an inception assessment and agreed assignment work plan covering priority activities, expected outputs, milestones, dependencies, counterpart responsibilities and the in-country and remote input schedule. Identify information gaps and specialist support needed, and maintain an action tracker as implementation progresses.
  • ii. National Payment Services Strategy implementation
  • Support NRBT to translate its five-year Strategy into a prioritised implementation plan. Specify responsibilities, timelines, resource requirements and dependencies, with a defined work programme for the first 12 months and a sequence for longer-term actions.
  • Review progress with NRBT and industry counterparts, help resolve implementation issues and prepare decision papers on priorities requiring management direction. Keep domestic actions aligned with the CBR Project and any preparatory actions arising from the PPM feasibility study.
  • iii. Payment system oversight and regulation
  • Support NRBT to strengthen its payments oversight function and prepare the operational arrangements needed under the evolving Payment Systems and Services framework. Activities may cover licensing or registration processes, reporting, risk-based monitoring, operational resilience, consumer protection and coordination with other NRBT functions.
  • Assist NRBT with payment oversight procedures, risk-monitoring tools, internal reporting and escalation arrangements. Advise on responsibilities for payment operations and oversight, and on safeguards to manage conflicts between those functions where relevant.
  • Provide payment system technical inputs to draft regulations, rules, circulars and guidance, working with legal counsel and relevant specialists. Legal drafting and formal legal opinions remain the responsibility of appropriately qualified legal counsel. Implementation advice must reflect the legislation and powers in force at the relevant time.
  • iv. Payment infrastructure and priority initiatives
  • Provide technical and implementation support for initiatives prioritised by NRBT under the Strategy. Confirm the initial initiatives, their stage of development and required support in the work plan; the assignment does not presume a particular infrastructure investment or technology solution.
  • Help define and review business requirements, options, project plans and payment-related procurement inputs. Advise on interoperability, payment messaging, participation arrangements, settlement and liquidity risks, security, business continuity and operational readiness, as relevant to each initiative.
  • Support implementation oversight, participant coordination, industry testing and readiness reviews. Document issues and recommended actions, and coordinate specialist technical inputs where needed. Vendors and participating institutions remain responsible for system development, configuration and defect correction.
  • v. Industry coordination and stakeholder engagement
  • Support regular engagement between NRBT, banks, payment service providers, money transfer operators, government agencies and other relevant participants. Strengthen existing consultation arrangements and help establish additional coordination mechanisms where NRBT identifies a need.
  • Prepare consultation materials, meeting agendas, minutes and action trackers. Support discussions on implementation responsibilities, public-sector payment needs and cross-institutional issues, with decisions and outstanding actions recorded for follow-up.
  • vi. Payments data and monitoring
  • Help NRBT strengthen the collection, analysis and use of payments data for oversight and policy. Agree priority indicators covering payment volumes and values, system availability, transaction failures, fraud, complaints, remittance flows and costs, and other measures required by NRBT.
  • Support the preparation or review of reporting templates, data definitions, validation checks and monitoring tools. Align country inputs with CBR Project and PPM data requests and, where feasible and agreed, support gender-disaggregated reporting on payment and financial-service usage.
  • vii. PPM feasibility study and regional coordination
  • Support NRBT's active participation in the PPM feasibility study by coordinating country data and stakeholder inputs, preparing NRBT for consultations and workshops, and reviewing draft findings and design options from Tonga's perspective.
  • Help NRBT identify the key requirements for possible future participation in the PPM as the proposed arrangement develops. Consider the relevant legal and regulatory, institutional, technical, operational and risk-management requirements, together with governance, resourcing and participant-readiness implications identified through the study.
  • Prepare and maintain a PPM participation requirements and prioritised action plan for NRBT. Map gaps, proposed actions, responsible institutions, dependencies and indicative timing, and incorporate agreed preparatory actions into the National Payment Services Strategy implementation plan. Requirements should be updated as the feasibility study develops; participation remains subject to its findings, the eventual arrangements and the relevant approvals.
  • Coordinate with the PIFS PMU, PIFS Payment Systems Specialist, World Bank payments team and other technical assistance providers on regional payment standards, cross-border payments, CBR information and harmonization activities. Help NRBT avoid duplication and sequence regional support with domestic work.
  1. Capacity building and knowledge transfer
  • Work directly with designated NRBT counterparts throughout the assignment, providing mentoring and on-the-job training in payment policy, operations, oversight, data analysis and implementation management, according to agreed needs.
  • Assess immediate and medium- to long-term training needs and prepare a multi-year capacity-building plan. Identify suitable training, peer-learning and regional exchange opportunities, and prepare practical templates, procedures and training materials that NRBT staff can continue to use.
  • Support handover of ongoing activities, tools and working documents, with named counterpart responsibilities and a record of remaining training and implementation needs.

 

Scope Exclusions

The assignment is limited to payment systems technical assistance. It does not include drafting primary legislation or formal legal opinions, general central banking advice unrelated to payments, or responsibility for production system development, procurement decisions or regulatory approvals. NRBT retains its statutory and decision-making responsibilities.

Detailed system design, cybersecurity testing, specialist supervisory manuals or other specialist work will be coordinated with appropriately qualified experts where required. Any material addition to the agreed scope or input ceiling will require written approval through the project arrangements.

Time-Based Reporting Obligations and Expected Outputs

This is a time-based individual consultant assignment. Payments will be linked to approved timesheets, agreed input days and eligible reimbursable expenses. The expected outputs are working products for managing implementation, reviewing the quality of advice and documenting knowledge transfer; they are not a fixed-price deliverables schedule.

Working products will include the inception assessment and assignment work plan; the prioritised National Payment Services Strategy implementation plan; oversight procedures and technical advisory notes; implementation and testing inputs for agreed payment initiatives; consultation materials and action trackers; payments data and monitoring tools; the PPM participation requirements and prioritised action plan; and training materials and the multi-year capacity-building plan.

Outputs may be revised or reprioritised with the agreement of NRBT, PIFS and the World Bank as implementation progresses. Changes will be recorded in progress notes and the action tracker. The Expert will submit a final completion and handover report covering work undertaken, materials produced, outstanding actions, risks and recommendations for continued implementation.

 

Reporting Obligations

The Expert will work for the NRBT's Assistant Governor Operations and designated payments staff on a day-to-day technical basis and administratively to the Project Coordinator in the PIFS PMU. Technical priorities, work planning and expected outputs will be agreed with NRBT, PIFS and the World Bank payments team. Coordination will also involve the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and Tonga Country Coordinator as relevant.

Monthly timesheets and short monthly activity notes will be submitted to the NRBT and the PIFS PMU confirming the principal activities undertaken. The notes will record days worked, in-country and remote inputs, meetings, outputs, implementation issues, decisions required and activities planned for the following month.

The Expert will update the action tracker at least monthly and submit quarterly progress notes against the agreed work plan. Technical outputs will be shared with NRBT and PIFS, with World Bank review or no-objection obtained where required under the project arrangements.

 

Institutional Arrangements

This is a time-based individual consultant assignment contracted by PIFS through the PMU under the Pacific Strengthening CBR Project. PIFS will contract the independent individual consultant through the PMU for the benefit of NRBT. The proposed term is up to 12 months and up to 240 working days, providing for a full-time level of input. This workload does not establish a requirement for continuous residence in Tonga.

The current planning assumption is that 50-60 percent of input days will be delivered in Tonga, working directly with NRBT in Nuku'alofa, with remote inputs used for document preparation, follow-up and coordination. NRBT must confirm whether this meets its requirements or whether a fully resident expert is required. The agreed arrangement and related budget must be settled before recruitment and stated consistently in the advertisement and contract.

NRBT will facilitate access to relevant documents, designated staff and industry participants. Office space and meeting facilities may be provided by NRBT for in-country inputs and by PIFS for agreed inputs in Suva, subject to availability. The Expert will maintain secure records and comply with confidentiality requirements.

Continuation or extension will be subject to performance, project needs, budget availability, procurement plan arrangements and applicable approvals. Performance reviews will assess the quality and timeliness of advisory support, counterpart engagement and knowledge transfer.

 

Performance Indicators

Performance assessment will focus on inputs, the quality of working products, implementation support and knowledge transfer within the agreed time-based work plan. The Expert will be assessed on the following:

  • Monthly timesheets and activity notes are submitted on time and accurately distinguish in-country and remote inputs, work undertaken, outputs and decisions required.
  • An inception assessment and assignment work plan are agreed, and a prioritised National Payment Services Strategy implementation plan is prepared and updated with NRBT.
  • An action tracker is maintained with activities, responsible counterparts, deadlines, dependencies, risks and pending decisions.
  • Payment oversight and regulatory implementation support is documented through technical notes, procedures, review comments or working materials, with specialist and legal matters referred appropriately.
  • Agreed payment initiatives receive documented support on requirements, planning, participant coordination, testing and operational readiness.
  • Industry engagement is documented through consultation materials, meeting notes and follow-up actions, and payments data work produces agreed templates or monitoring tools.
  • NRBT receives timely support for PPM consultations, country inputs and review of study findings. A PPM participation requirements and prioritised action plan is prepared and kept aligned with the study and NRBT's implementation priorities.
  • Training and mentoring are documented, immediate and longer-term skills needs are assessed, and a multi-year capacity-building plan is prepared.
  • Quarterly progress notes and a final completion and handover report are submitted, identifying completed work, outstanding actions, open risks and counterpart responsibilities.
  • Advice remains professional, objective and impartial, input days are recorded accurately, and the Expert complies with confidentiality, conflict-of-interest and anti-fraud requirements.

Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The Expert will comply with NRBT’s statutory requirements, including all applicable confidentiality, secrecy, data protection and information-protection obligations, as well as relevant PIFS and World Bank policies and rules on anti-corruption, prevention of fraudulent practices, conflicts of interest and confidentiality. Sensitive information obtained during the assignment will be kept confidential and handled only for the purposes of the assignment. Findings, data, reports and recommendations must not be published or disclosed without prior written consent from NRBT and PIFS, and World Bank clearance where required.

Draft reports and other documents will be reviewed and cleared through the agreed NRBT, PIFS and World Bank arrangements before final issue. A non-disclosure agreement may be signed and attached to the contract. Documents and data will be stored, transmitted and handled securely in accordance with NRBT’s applicable statutory and information-protection requirements and the contractual provisions of the assignment, and transferred to the designated counterparts at handover.

Actual or potential conflicts of interest must be disclosed before contract signature and throughout the assignment. The Expert must not participate in downstream procurement where this would create a conflict under the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations or Project Operations Manual.

In order to ensure the effective implementation of Package II (Quality Monitoring, Inspection and Evaluation Services) under the above-mentioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Demonstration Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to apply for a World Bank loan of USD10,000,000. Of this amount, Package II (Quality Monitoring, Inspection and Evaluation Services) under the abovementioned project plans to apply for a World Bank loan of USD 29.42 million (equivalent to RMB 2.03 million). It will provide targeted support for the achievement of project objectives through the following deliverables: engage a thirdparty institution to carry out quality monitoring, inspection and evaluation services; conduct quality monitoring of high-quality food in accordance with the inspection and testing requirements specified in high-quality food standards (including sensory requirements, quality indicators and partial safety indicators, with no fewer than 700 batches monitored within two years); and conduct on-site inspection and evaluation of high-quality food enterprises (no fewer than 20 enterprises covered within two years).

Expected outcomes of this project include tracking and evaluating the quality and safety status of high-quality food; ensuring that manufacturing and trading enterprises of high-quality food as well as the high-quality food products themselves consistently comply with the requirements of high-quality food standards; establishing and maintaining the credibility of high-quality food brands; and enhancing consumer trust in high-quality food.

2.Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of advancing quality monitoring, inspection and evaluation services, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel under market regulation. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as“proportion of early-warnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". The core objectives are to build a premium brand image of high-quality food, to formulate evaluation and management specifications for high-quality food, to utilize multiple approaches including on-site inspection and evaluation and quality monitoring to track and evaluate the quality and safety status of high-quality food, thereby comprehensively safeguarding quality and safety of high-quality food, and promoting the improvement of food quality and the high-quality development of the food industry.

3.1 Scope of Service Recipients

Specific work contents are as follows:  First, conduct quality monitoring of high-quality food in accordance with the requirements of Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation and based on the test items and test methods specified in high-quality food standards. Testing items shall include sensory requirements, quality indicators, and partial safety indicators. The contractor shall perform statistical analysis on the test results, assess whether the results comply with the requirements of the high-quality food standards, and issue a test report. The testing institution shall formulate an annual sampling plan, ensuring that the sampled products cover as many categories of high-quality food as possible. No fewer than 700 batches shall be monitored within two years. Second, the contractor shall organize on-site inspections of high-quality food manufacturing and trading entities, and conduct evaluations on the whole process, including supplier management, base management, quality management at key control points for production and operation, warehousing and logistics management, personnel management, and system development of enterprises, so as to ensure that high-quality food products consistently meet the standard requirements. The inspection institution shall formulate an annual inspection and evaluation plan, aiming to cover as many implementing entities as possible. No fewer than 20 enterprises shall be covered within two years . Where quality monitoring or on-site inspection confirms that an enterprise or product fails to comply with high-quality food standards but meets food safety standards, the relevant information shall be promptly reported to the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation. The relevant products shall be removed from the special sales zones for high-quality food, and the “Greater Bay Area Standard”logo on product outer packaging shall be revoked. By coordinating the sampling layout across both online and offline channels, a comprehensive and multi-dimensional supervision system can be established, so as to effectively ensure that consumers can obtain authentic, safe and highquality product experience when purchasing high-quality food through any channels.

(3) Test items

Test items shall strictly comply with the relevant provisions on inspection and testing specified in high-quality food standards,ensuring comprehensive coverage of the three core aspects explicitly required: first, sensory requirements—including the color, odor, taste, and texture of high-quality foods, which are visually distinguishable characteristics designed to ensure that the product meets consumers' sensory expectations for high quality; second, quality indicators—such as moisture content, fat content, protein content, peroxide value, and soluble solids—which are key parameters reflecting the intrinsic quality of the product and guarantee its authenticity and superior quality; third, the selection of safety indicators shall be based on risk assessment results, covering limit values for substances that may affect human health, such as heavy metals (e.g., lead, cadmium, arsenic), mycotoxins (e.g., aflatoxins), pesticide residues, and the levels of food additive usage. These approaches ensures that high-quality foods not only meet stringent quality requirements but also provide adequate safety assurance.

2

Inspection and Evaluation of high-quality food enterprises in accordance with the requirements of the project (no fewer than 20 enterprises covered within two years)

  1. Priority inspection targets

Priority shall be given to the inspection and evaluation of enterprises falling under any of the following categories: enterprises whose food products manufactured have no records of non-compliance or failure in supervision samplinginspection or high-quality food quality monitoring over the past two years; enterprises classified as Level-C or Level-D by the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation in accordance with the Measures for Risk-based Classification Management of Food and Food-Related Product Manufacturers of Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation (Trial); enterprises whose products are newly included in the high-quality food list in the current year; and enterprises that have not been connected to the high-quality food traceability platform

(2) Key inspection content

Enterprise inspections shall cover key links across the whole chain of high-quality food production, storage, transportation, and sales chain, including raw material control (e.g., supplier qualification review and raw material base management), key control points during the production process (e.g., real-time record of process parameters such as processing temperature and duration),  authenticity of traceability data (cross-check against data from high-quality food traceability platforms), and the usage of the "GBA Standard" logo; so as to ensure full process control from source to customers.

Assignment Title:

Consultancy Services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul

Reference No.: GM-NAWEC-565968-CS-QCBS

The Republic of The Gambia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul.

The Greater Banjul Area is the country’s principal urban and economic center. Urban water services face major challenges including production constraints, intermittent supply, ageing infrastructure, limited storage capacity, and high levels of non-revenue water. Similarly, sanitation services in Banjul and Kotu are constrained by deteriorated sewerage assets, underperforming wastewater treatment facilities, and inadequate fecal sludge management infrastructure.  WASAP will support the Government of The Gambia in addressing these challenges through investments aimed at improving service coverage, reliability, resilience, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation services.

The assignment will support the preparation and implementation of priority investments in urban water supply and urban sanitation infrastructure, including:

  • Urban water supply investments in Kombo East and Brikama East comprising boreholes, treatment facilities, storage reservoirs, transmission pipelines, distribution networks, household connections, SCADA systems, and power supply facilities; and
  • Urban sanitation investments including rehabilitation and expansion of wastewater and sewerage infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul, fecal sludge treatment facilities, pumping stations, and associated infrastructure.

Scope of the Services

The consulting services will be undertaken in five phases:

Phase 1: Feasibility Study

  • Review existing studies, plans, records, GIS data and infrastructure information.
  • Conduct socio-economic, service area, demand and affordability assessments.
  • Undertake detailed feasibility studies for urban water supply and sanitation investments.
  • Assess climate resilience, environmental and social requirements, institutional arrangements, technical options and implementation strategies.
  • Conduct economic and financial analyses, including lifecycle costing and investment prioritization.
  • Prepare feasibility reports and preliminary designs.

Phase 2: Detailed Engineering Design

  • Undertake topographic, cadastral, geotechnical, laboratory and utility investigations.
  • Prepare detailed engineering designs for:
    • Water supply facilities including boreholes, treatment systems, reservoirs, transmission mains, distribution networks and SCADA.
    • Sanitation facilities include wastewater treatment systems, fecal sludge treatment plants, sewer networks, pumping stations and sea outfall improvements.
  • Prepare design calculations, drawings, technical specifications, cost estimates, bills of quantities, and O&M documentation.
  • Prepare procurement-ready engineering packages.

Phase 3: Procurement Support

  • Prepare complete bidding documents and technical specifications.
  • Participate in pre-bid meetings and site visits.
  • Provide support during bid evaluation and contract award processes.
  • Respond to technical clarifications and prepare addenda where required.

Phase 4: Construction Supervision and Contract Administration

  • Supervise construction works and administer contracts.
  • Monitor quality assurance, environmental and social compliance, occupational health and safety, cost and schedule performance.
  • Review contractor submissions and oversee testing and commissioning.
  • Support handover and completion.

Phase 5: Defects Liability Support

  • Conduct inspections during the defect’s liability period.
  • Verify correction of defects.
  • Support final completion and contract close-out.

Duration

The estimated duration of the assignment is 46.5 months, including feasibility studies, design, procurement support, construction supervision, and defects liability support.

Assignment Title: Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/08

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. ”Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

NRA has developed and operates a Road Asset Management System (RAMS). However, there are still many unresolved issues that prevent the proper use of the RAMS as a key pillar for the further effective road investment and maintenance planning processes, such as: lack of integration/interoperability of sub systems; manual intensive data collection; fragmentation of roles in RAMS related data collection and utilization; non-clear future alignment with the road register; lack of the sufficient legal regulation.

NRA intends to retain a consultant to lay the strategic, technical, institutional, and legal groundwork for the modernization of NRA's Road Asset Management System, so that Moldova's national road network can be managed efficiently, cost-effectively, and in line with European standards. Specifically, consultant will be required to review business processes and recommend improvements; review of existing IT based tools, software, databases, etc. architecture and integration and recommendations for further improvement preparation; develop a future RAMS Roadmap; define the asset inventory scope and data governance framework required for the future RAMS; Policy Framework Development; develop a training program and conduct a number of in-person workshops covering mentioned above topics.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria:

The following shortlisting criteria will be applied to all consulting firms (individual company or joint venture overall) that have submitted EoI:

1. Criterion: General Firm Experience

Proven general experience and verifiable track record in providing consultancy/technical assistance related to Road Asset Management Systems (RAMSs), completed within the past ten (10) years. RAMS-related consultancy/technical assistance may cover studies; strategies; policy frameworks; institutional support; or preparation of methodologies, guidelines, and standards.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

2. Criterion: Development or implementation of RAMS solutions

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to development or implementation of the existing RAMS solutions, deployed on local and/or national road networks with paved and unpaved roads, completed within the past ten (10) years. For the purpose of this criterion, an assignment shall be considered completed if the RAMS solution has been fully developed and/or deployed and formally accepted by the client, regardless of subsequent maintenance or update activities.

Preference will be given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 40 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

3. Criterion: Road network data

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 30 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

4. Criterion: Training

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in delivering training related to RAMS completed within the last ten (10) years, with preference given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 10 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

As a proof, the Consultant shall prepare a table listing following information: name of the relevant assignments, year of contract’s implementation (start year, end year), information on contract value, length of road network covered, percentage carried out by Consultant in case of association of firms and short description of main activities, contracting entity/client, country/region, contact reference (name, e-mail, phone number).

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.
